finding.title: NMP post-capture R+1 cites a consensus that no longer exists (variable mismatch with Obsidian's ttMoveNoisy)
finding.claim: Coda adds R+=1 to NMP when the PREVIOUS move was a capture, with the comment '(Consensus: SF/Obsidian increase R after captures, not decrease)'. Neither claim holds against current sources: SF's R is now flat `7 + depth/3` (search.cpp:919) with no capture term of any kind, and Obsidian's extra reduction is `R += ttMoveNoisy` — keyed to the CURRENT node's TT move being noisy (a 'this node is tactical and the TT already knows the refutation' signal), not to the parent move having been a capture. None of the 6 references condition NMP R on the previous move being a capture. Coda did empirically test the OPPOSITE direction (R-1 after captures, H0 at experiments.md:1333, and a V5-era R-1 merge at :2159), so the +1 direction has some history, but the stated consensus justification is stale and the nearest real consensus analog uses a different variable (tt_move_noisy, which Coda already computes at 3460-3464). Low priority; mechanism for gain is that ttMoveNoisy fires on a genuinely different (and per Obsidian, better-calibrated) set of nodes than prev-capture.
finding.evidence: Coda search.rs:3662-3666 `// Reduce more after captures: opponent just captured... (Consensus: SF/Obsidian increase R after captures, not decrease) if !board.undo_stack.is_empty() && board.undo_stack[...].captured != NO_PIECE_TYPE { r += 1; }`. Stockfish search.cpp:919 `Depth R = 7 + depth / 3;` (no capture/tt term). Obsidian search.cpp:882 `int R = std::min((eval - beta) / NmpEvalDiv, (int)NmpEvalDivMin) + depth / NmpDepthDiv + NmpBase + ttMoveNoisy;` where ttMoveNoisy (line 733) is the current node's TT move. Reckless search.rs:547, PlentyChess search.cpp:836, Alexandria search.cpp:576, Berserk search.c:536: none have a prev-capture term.
finding.expected_impact: quality / +0-1 Elo probe
finding.suggested_change: Fix the stale comment; cheap probe: replace the prev-capture condition with `tt_move_noisy` (Obsidian's variable, already computed at 3460) or test removal, SPRT [-2,1]. Do not treat as a bug — both directions have SPRT history.

(2) OB #1067 `experiment/nmp-no-prev-cap-bonus` (2026-05-10): REMOVAL of the r+=1 term = H0 -2.6 ±3.0; entry explicitly states "Cross-engine 'consensus' citation in commit 2da11be was inaccurate (Obsidian uses ttMoveNoisy of CURRENT node, not previous-move-was-capture), but the term works. Possible follow-up: port Obsidian's ttMoveNoisy as separate experiment." (3) That follow-up was then run FOUR times: #732 nmp-ttnoisy-rplus H0 -0.4 @ 41K; #754 re-SPRT on post-tune-750 trunk H0 -0.8; #768 v3 (guard + retune) H0 -0.5 @ 44.4K; #2270 nmp-tt-capture-guard (2026-06-25 NMP audit, N5, [-1.5,1.5]) flat +0.3 ±1.3 @ 76K, dropped — "Coda's NMP is reliable enough without it." verdict.reasoning: Every factual element of the finding checks out. Code (src/search.rs:3662-3666): the comment "(Consensus: SF/Obsidian increase R after captures, not decrease)" sits on a `board.undo_stack[last].captured != NO_PIECE_TYPE → r += 1` condition, exactly as claimed. Spot-checked engines: Stockfish search.cpp:919 is flat `Depth R = 7 + depth / 3` with no capture/TT term; Obsidian search.cpp:733/882 has `ttMoveNoisy = ttMove && !pos.isQuiet(ttMove)` added to R — CURRENT-node TT move, not prev-capture. So the comment does cite a consensus that doesn't exist, and the variable mismatch with Obsidian is real. HOWEVER, the reviewer's own "cheap probe" suggestions are both exhaustively dead: (a) removal of the prev-capture r+=1 was SPRT'd at #1067 and H0'd (-2.6) — the term empirically defends itself and was originally banked at +3.5 with retune (exp #195); (b) the ttMoveNoisy port has been tried FOUR times (#732, #754, #768, #2270), including #2270 just 6 days ago in the 2026-06-25 NMP audit — i.e. AFTER the +116 Elo of June gains, so "circumstances changed" does not justify a fifth retest — and it came back flat at 76K games. The #1067 experiments.md entry even documented the exact same Obsidian-variable-mismatch observation in May, but the code comment was never corrected. What survives is precisely the reviewer's lowest-value component: fix the stale comment (docs-only, zero Elo, no bench change, no SPRT needed). Verdict is confirmed because the claim as written is accurate and the reviewer correctly hedged ("do not treat as a bug"), but the actionable experiment space is fully explored and dead — the only remaining action is a one-line comment edit at src/search.rs:3663 noting the term is empirically validated (#195 H1, #1067 removal H0) rather than consensus-derived.

finding.title: NMP undefended-count precomputation misses the cut_node/nmp_min_ply gates and runs before razor/RFP
finding.claim: The `undefended_count` block computes `board.attacks_by_color(board.side_to_move)` (a second full setwise attack map, comparable in cost to enemy_attacks) behind a 'cheap gate' (`nmp_gate_cheap`) whose stated purpose is 'Only bother computing when NMP might actually fire'. But the gate replicates only part of the real NMP gate at 3650-3657: it omits `cut_node` (NMP is hard-gated to expected cut nodes at 3656 — roughly half of ZW nodes can NEVER fire NMP), `ply >= info.nmp_min_ply` (verification subtrees), and `FEAT_NMP`. Worse, the whole block sits BEFORE the razoring+RFP block (3551-3643), so every RFP cutoff node with static_eval >= beta+margin first pays the full own-side attack map for an NMP that is then never reached (RFP returns at 3640). Since RFP runs first precisely because it is the free static prune (comment at 3546-3550), paying an attack-map computation before it inverts that economy. The computation is used only in nmp_threat_margin (3648) and the NMP-eligibility comparison — both after RFP.
finding.evidence: search.rs:3528-3540: `let nmp_gate_cheap = depth >= tp10(&NMP_MIN_DEPTH_10X) && !in_check && ply > 0 && stm_non_pawn != 0 && beta - alpha == 1 && static_eval >= beta && !prev_was_null && beta.abs() < MATE_IN_MAX_PLY && info.excluded_move[ply_u] == NO_MOVE; if nmp_gate_cheap && tp10(&NMP_UNDEFENDED_MAX_10X) > 0 { ... let our_attacks = board.attacks_by_color(board.side_to_move); popcount(attacked & !our_attacks) as i32 }`. Real NMP gate at 3650-3657 additionally requires `ply >= info.nmp_min_ply` and `&& cut_node // Reckless gate: only attempt NMP at expected fail-high nodes` and `FEAT_NMP`. The block is at 3528, the RFP return at 3640 — so RFP-cut nodes (`static_eval - margin >= beta` implies the cheap gate's `static_eval >= beta` passed) always paid it first.
finding.expected_impact: NPS-only, small (~0.5-1% NPS); trivially bundleable with the enemy_attacks/xray reorder finding into one [-2,1] SPRT
finding.suggested_change: Move the undefended_count block to just above nmp_threat_margin (~line 3645, i.e. after the razor/RFP block) and add `&& cut_node && ply >= info.nmp_min_ply` to nmp_gate_cheap. Behavior-identical (bench nodes unchanged) since the value is only consumed by the NMP gate that already requires those conditions.

verdict.reasoning: Verified in src/search.rs. The cheap gate (3530-3534) genuinely omits cut_node, ply>=nmp_min_ply, and FEAT_NMP, all required by the real NMP gate (3650-3657); the cut_node omission means the all-node half of gate-passing ZW nodes compute attacks_by_color for a value that is never consumed. The block (3528) sits before the razor/RFP block (3551-3643): RFP-cut nodes (static_eval - margin >= beta implies the gate's static_eval >= beta) always pay it first, and the depth overlap is wide (NMP min depth ~5 via NMP_MIN_DEPTH_10X=51, RFP_DEPTH=18). The comment at 3546-3549 shows RFP was deliberately moved before NMP in #1882 but the precompute was left behind — a stale-order artifact. Behavior-identical claim checks out: undefended_count is consumed only via nmp_threat_margin (3645-3648) in the NMP condition (3651), which already requires cut_node/nmp_min_ply/FEAT_NMP; nothing between 3544 and 3645 reads it. One correction: razor-cut nodes never pay the cost (razor needs eval <= alpha - mult*depth, incompatible with eval >= beta), so only the RFP path matters. attacks_by_color (board.rs:533) is the same setwise function as enemy_attacks (3019), so the cost comparison is literally correct, but it is cheap (setwise, not per-square magic), and the eligible node slice (non-check, ZW, depth>=5, eval>=beta) is small — realistic saving is likely <0.5% NPS, below the reviewer's 0.5-1% estimate. Prior experiments (#617/#676 added the feature, H1; #1063 gate-removal H0 — feature is real signal, keep it) never tested placement/gate economy. Real but marginal NPS-only fix; bundle into a [-2,1] SPRT as suggested.

finding.title: Missing TT-score refinement of eval before whole-node pruning (6/6 unanimous)
finding.claim: Coda computes static_eval = corrected(scaled(raw_eval)) and feeds it directly to razoring (3562), RFP (3599), and the NMP gate + NMP eval-R term (3651, 3667) without first tightening it with the TT score when the stored bound direction agrees. All 6 reference engines refine the local pruning eval this way immediately after computing corrected eval, so their whole-node pruning runs on search-verified information instead of a bare static eval: sounder cutoffs where TT says the position is better than eval, and suppressed unsound cutoffs where a TT upper bound says it is worse. Coda already merged the exact QS analog (fix-qs-tt-stand-pat, +6.5 H1, search.rs:5219-5238, whose comment even says 'consensus: every top engine does this') but the main-search site is missing. CAVEAT: a 2026-03-12 attempt logged -77 Elo/174g, but that was 4 months and several hundred self-play Elo ago on the pre-fix engine, it added a non-consensus ttDepth>=depth-3 gate, and its rationale ('Stockfish only adjusts the improving flag, not the eval itself') is factually wrong — SF replaces eval itself at search.cpp:749-752. The catastrophic magnitude suggests the old version leaked the refined value into the static_evals stack / corrhist / improving baseline. Correct port: refine a SEPARATE local (Reckless's estimated_score) used only by razor/RFP/NMP(/futility) gates; keep info.static_evals[ply], corrhist updates, and TT eval stores on the pure corrected static eval; no depth gate; guard decisive scores.
finding.evidence: Coda search.rs:3416 `static_eval = ... corrected_eval(info, board, scaled_eval) ...` then straight to razor `static_eval + tp(&RAZOR_MULT) * depth <= alpha` (3562), RFP `static_eval - margin >= beta` (3599), NMP `static_eval >= beta + nmp_threat_margin` (3651) — no TT refinement anywhere in between. References, all on the refine side: Stockfish search.cpp:749-752 `if (is_valid(ttData.value) && (ttData.bound & (ttData.value > eval ? BOUND_LOWER : BOUND_UPPER))) eval = ttData.value;`; Reckless search.rs:424-436 `estimated_score = tt_score` (fed to razor:504, RFP:515-517, NMP:532); Obsidian search.cpp:835-837 `if (ttScore != SCORE_NONE && canUseScore(ttBound, ttScore, eval)) eval = ttScore;`; Berserk search.c:476-477 `if (ttScore != UNKNOWN && (ttBound & (ttScore > eval ? BOUND_LOWER : BOUND_UPPER))) eval = ttScore;`; PlentyChess search.cpp:752-753 same three-bound form; Alexandria search.cpp:507-509 `if (ttScore != SCORE_NONE && (ttBound & (ttScore >= eval ? HFLOWER : HFUPPER))) eval = ttScore;`. Coda's own QS analog: search.rs:5219-5238 (merged H1 +6.5, experiments.md:3823).
finding.expected_impact: +2-5 Elo class (likely with retune-on-branch; QS analog banked +6.5)
finding.suggested_change: After line 3416, add `let mut estimated_eval = static_eval;` and refine it from tt_entry (score_from_tt, bound-direction check, abs() < MATE_IN_MAX_PLY guard, no depth gate). Use estimated_eval in razor (3562), RFP (3582/3599), NMP entry gate + eval-R term (3651/3667-3669); leave info.static_evals[ply_u], improving, unstable, corrhist, and all TT stores on static_eval/raw_eval. SPRT [0,3].

Engine citations spot-checked in 4 of 6 references and all accurate: Stockfish replaces the local eval (keeping ss->staticEval pure — matching the reviewer's proposed port); Reckless builds estimated_score at search.rs:424-448 and feeds razor:504/RFP:514-524/NMP:532-547; Berserk search.c:476-477 and Obsidian search.cpp:835-837 match. Porting notes for the retest: Reckless additionally gates NMP on estimated_score >= eval (line 533), worth copying; the abs()<MATE_IN_MAX_PLY guard is load-bearing because Coda's eval-only TT stubs store score=-INFINITY with UPPER flag (same hazard the QS site already handles); consider the QS site's halfmove < TT_CUTOFF_HALFMOVE_MAX guard for parity; keep static_evals/improving/corrhist/TT stores on the pure corrected eval. Given three prior fails in the family, expect this may need retune-on-branch and possibly an in-check/excluded-move gate like Reckless; SPRT [0,3] as suggested.

finding.title: NMP returns unproven TB-win scores: mate clamp uses MATE_IN_MAX_PLY, not the decisive (TB-inclusive) bound
finding.claim: On a null-move fail-high, the score clamp `if null_score.abs() > MATE_IN_MAX_PLY { beta }` only catches mate-range scores (|s| > 28872). Tablebase scores (TB_WIN - ply, i.e. 28672..28800, all BELOW MATE_IN_MAX_PLY=28872) pass through unclamped, so with Syzygy loaded (the lichess deployment regime) NMP can return an unproven TB-win as the node score: 'even after passing, a TB probe in the reduced null subtree said we win' is not proof the side to move wins, exactly like an unproven mate. Coda's own tt.rs doc (599-606) exists for this trap: 'The widespread |s| < MATE_IN_MAX_PLY ... mate guards admit TB scores ... use this [is_decisive] where TB scores must also be excluded (SF/Reckless/Stormphrax is_decisive; 2026-06-11 audit T2.3)'. Stockfish clamps at the TB boundary ('Do not return unproven mate or TB scores': if nullValue >= VALUE_TB_WIN_IN_MAX_PLY, nullValue = beta). Minor secondary nit in the same line: the comparison is strict `>`, so a deepest-ply mate at exactly |s| == MATE_IN_MAX_PLY also escapes the clamp. Impact is confined to TB-enabled play near TB-decisive nodes (OB runs without TB), hence low expected magnitude — but the fix is one token and removes a real inconsistency at the deployment target.
finding.evidence:
search.rs:3699-3702: `if null_score >= beta { // Return null score directly ... // Clamp mate scores to beta to avoid inflated mate distance
 let nmp_score = if null_score.abs() > MATE_IN_MAX_PLY { beta } else { null_score };` — with tt.rs constants MATE_SCORE=29000, TB_WIN=28800, MATE_IN_MAX_PLY=MATE_SCORE-128=28872, and tt.rs:605-607 `pub fn is_decisive(score: i32) -> bool { score.abs() >= TB_WIN - 200 }` documented explicitly as the TB-inclusive guard for cases like this. TB scores are produced in-search at 3097-3100 (`TB_WIN - ply` / `-TB_WIN + ply`), so they do occur inside null subtrees when tablebases are loaded. Stockfish: 'Do not return unproven mate or TB scores' — clamps nullValue at VALUE_TB_WIN_IN_MAX_PLY.
finding.expected_impact: correctness at deployment (TB-enabled lichess/CCRL); ~0 Elo at OB STC/LTC (no TB), so ship under [-2,1] or bundle with another change
finding.suggested_change: Replace the clamp with `let nmp_score = if is_decisive(null_score) { beta } else { null_score };` (imports already available via crate::tt::is_decisive; it is used at line 3862 in ProbCut).

(2) #1941 atlas/multicut-no-decisive H1 +1.6 ±2.5 (2026-06-13 audit T1.4) — fixed the same unproven-mate/TB-score trap in multicut and introduced tt::is_decisive for it. (3) Corrhist overhaul T2.3 applied is_decisive TB gate. Same trap-class fixed twice elsewhere with H1s; NMP site never addressed.

No neutralizing guard exists: the NMP gate beta.abs() < MATE_IN_MAX_PLY admits TB-range betas; the zugzwang verification search proves only >= beta at reduced depth and still returns the raw nmp_score; below verify-depth the score is returned immediately. Coda's own tt.rs docs (589-591, 600-606) explicitly name this trap and is_decisive is already used for it at ProbCut (3862), SE (4101), and qsearch/corrhist T2.3 (4884) — this NMP site is the stragglers. Cross-engine citations spot-checked and correct in substance: Stockfish search.cpp:926 'Do not return unproven mate or TB scores' gates the NMP cutoff on !is_win(nullValue) with is_win = v >= VALUE_TB_WIN_IN_MAX_PLY (types.h:170-172); Reckless search.rs:565 identically gates on !is_win(score) with is_win = score >= TB_WIN_IN_MAX. One corrected detail: current SF/Reckless skip the NMP cutoff entirely for win-scores rather than clamping to beta (the reviewer cited the older SF clamp-to-beta form); Coda's existing convention for mates is clamp-to-beta, so the suggested one-token fix (is_decisive(null_score) -> beta) is the minimal consistent extension, though the SF/Reckless 'skip cutoff' shape is the stronger consensus port if ever tested. The secondary strict-> nit is technically real (a mate at exactly ply=MAX_PLY scores exactly 28872 and escapes; is_mate_score uses >=) but is boundary-negligible. Priority low because the path is unreachable in OB SPRT/SPSA (no TB on fleet), so expected measured Elo ~0; it matters only at TB-enabled deployment (lichess/CCRL) near TB-decisive nodes, where positions are usually already winning/losing decisively. finding.title: ProbCut child searches run with stale moved_piece_stack/moved_to_stack (cont-hist corruption)
finding.claim: The ProbCut move loop makes a capture and searches the child at ply+1 (quiescence, then negamax) WITHOUT writing the capture into info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u]/moved_to_stack[ply_u]. Every other child-search site sets these: the regular moves loop (~4172), the NMP null search sets a 0-sentinel (~3701, the 'C3' audit fix), the RFP-audit null (~3642), and QS evasions (~5146). The ProbCut child therefore reads a STALE (piece,to) pair — whatever the last-visited sibling subtree at this same ply left in the slot (an unrelated move from a completely different position), or the 0-sentinel only if NMP happened to run at this node. The stale pair is used at ply+1 as the 1-ply continuation-history context: (a) negamax (~3897) loads prev_piece_for_cont from moved_piece_stack[ply_u-1] and feeds it to MovePicker quiet ordering, and (b) on beta cutoffs inside the ProbCut verification subtree, cont-hist bonuses/maluses are WRITTEN to info.history.cont_hist[stale_piece][stale_to][...] (~4569 with off=1, likewise ~4694/~4740), polluting the shared continuation-history table for the rest of the search; (c) if the ProbCut capture gives check, the child qsearch evasion picker also reads the stale slot for ordering. Note ProbCut typically fires exactly when NMP did NOT run (ProbCut targets static_eval < beta + margin nodes, NMP requires static_eval >= beta + nmp_threat_margin), so the common case is stale garbage, not the benign 0-sentinel. Concrete path: node A at ply 5 searches move Nf3-e5 (slot[5]=(N,e5)), returns; sibling node B at ply 5 (different position) enters, NMP gate fails (eval < beta), ProbCut makes QxR and searches the child at ply 6 — the child orders quiets and updates cont-hist keyed to (N,e5), a move that was never played on this path. Stockfish sets ss->currentMove and ss->continuationHistory inside its ProbCut loop before searching for exactly this reason.
finding.evidence: ProbCut loop (verified in current source ~3820-3838): `if let Some(acc) = &mut info.nnue_acc { acc.push(pc_dirty); } ... if !board.make_move(mv) { ... continue; }` then quiescence/negamax at ply+1 — no moved_piece_stack write anywhere in the loop. Verified grep of all moved_piece_stack writes in the file: only lines 3642 (RFP-audit null), 3701 (NMP null 0-sentinel), 4172 (moves loop), 5146 and 5357 (QS). Contrast the moves loop at ~4172: `info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u] = go_piece(moved_piece) as u8; info.moved_to_stack[ply_u] = to;`, and the NMP null site's own comment: 'Without this, child at ply+1 reads stale (piece, to) from a prior sibling move at this ply, feeding cont-hist ... with unrelated data.' Reader at ~3897: `let gp = info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u - 1] as usize;` (probcut child's ply_u-1 == this node's ply_u). Writer at ~4569: `let prior_piece = info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u - off] as usize; ... update_cont_history(&mut info.history.cont_hist[prior_piece][prior_to][...], bonus)`. Stockfish sets ss->currentMove + ss->continuationHistory inside its ProbCut loop before the child search.
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness; plausibly +1-3 Elo (stops active pollution of the shared cont-hist tables from every ProbCut attempt subtree); SPRT [0,3]
finding.suggested_change: After `board.make_move(mv)` succeeds in the ProbCut loop (before the quiescence call), mirror the moves-loop write: capture the colored piece before make_move (`let pc_moved_piece = board.piece_at(move_from(mv));`) and set `info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u] = go_piece(pc_moved_piece) as u8; info.moved_to_stack[ply_u] = move_to(mv);` (guarded by ply_u <= MAX_PLY). No restore needed — NMP and the moves loop overwrite the slot before their own children.

The ProbCut loop (3806-3867) pushes NNUE/threat state and calls quiescence+negamax at ply+1 but never writes moved_piece_stack[ply_u]/moved_to_stack[ply_u]; grep confirms the only writers are 3628 (RFP-audit null), 3687 (NMP null 0-sentinel, the C3 fix), 4158 (moves loop), 5132/5343 (QS evasions). The child at ply+1 reads the stale slot at 3883 (prev_piece_for_cont for MovePicker quiet ordering), at 3235-3238 (TT-cutoff cont-hist malus), and via the QS evasion picker (5093-5096) if the capture checks; on cutoffs in the verification subtree it WRITES cont_hist[stale_piece][stale_to][...] at 4555/4680/4726 (off=1 spans the ProbCut ply), polluting the shared table for the rest of the search. The gp!=0 guard only helps when the slot happens to hold the NMP 0-sentinel. One detail correction: Coda's ProbCut has no static_eval<beta+margin gate (removed in the fix-probcut revival), so the reviewer's stated NMP/ProbCut exclusion mechanism is wrong — but the conclusion holds via Coda's actual NMP gate (cut_node && zero-window && static_eval >= beta+threat_margin, lines 3650-3656): ProbCut runs at all non-PV nodes including all-nodes where NMP never fires, so the stale-garbage case is common. finding.title: Quiet-malus loop assumes the cutoff move is the last recorded quiet — wrong for non-capture-promotion cutoffs and on 64-entry saturation
finding.claim: quiets_tried records only `!is_cap && !is_promo` moves (4277), but the beta-cutoff branch selects on `!is_cap` alone (4638), and the malus loop `for i in 0..quiets_count.saturating_sub(1)` (4707) excludes the LAST recorded entry on the assumption it is the cutoff move. Trace: node where quiet moves A,B are searched and fail, then a non-capture promotion P (is_cap=false, is_promo=true — never recorded) causes the cutoff. Branch taken: quiet-history branch; quiets_count=2; loop runs i in 0..1 — only A is penalized, and B (a genuinely failed quiet) silently escapes its malus even though it is not the cutoff move. Same escape occurs whenever quiets_count saturated at 64 before the cutoff quiet was reached. Secondary wrinkle: the promotion P receives the full quiet main/cont/pawn-history BONUS chain (4666+) although the movepicker scores promotions in the captures stream (movegen.rs:138-143 puts push-promotions in generate_captures), so the bonus lands in a history slot no quiet-ordering path conflicts with (pawn-to-8th from/to is promo-only) — mostly benign, but the missed malus is a real, if rare, history-signal error.
finding.evidence: Recording: search.rs:4277 `if !is_cap && !is_promo && quiets_count < 64 { quiets_tried[quiets_count] = mv; ... }`. Branch: 4638 `if !is_cap {`. Malus: 4706-4708 `for i in 0..quiets_count.saturating_sub(1) { let q = quiets_tried[i]; ... -malus`. The `-1` is only correct when mv was recorded as the last entry, which fails for is_promo cutoffs and saturation.
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness, tiny magnitude (non-capture-promo cutoffs and 65+-quiet nodes are rare); bundle with another history change rather than solo-SPRT.
finding.suggested_change: Make the exclusion explicit instead of positional: loop `for i in 0..quiets_count { let q = quiets_tried[i]; if q == mv { continue; } ... }` — correct in all cases (recorded-or-not, saturated-or-not) at negligible cost.

(2) Cutoff branch at 4638 selects on `!is_cap` alone (is_cap defined at 3971 as piece-on-to || EP, so a push-promotion is !is_cap), so a non-capture promotion takes the full quiet bonus chain (main 4666, cont 4677-4694, pawn 4698). (3) Malus loop at 4707 is `for i in 0..quiets_count.saturating_sub(1)` — a purely positional exclusion that is only correct when the cutoff move was recorded as the last entry. For a promo cutoff (never recorded) or a quiet cutoff after 64-entry saturation, the last genuinely-failed quiet escapes its malus. The reviewer's trace is exact.

Two strong corroborations the reviewer didn't cite: (a) the CAPTURE malus loop 30 lines below (search.rs:4798) does `let cap_count = if is_cap { n_captures_tried.saturating_sub(1) } else { n_captures_tried };` — i.e. the codebase already knows the trailing-entry exclusion must be conditional on whether the cutoff move was recorded, and does it for captures but not quiets. finding.title: LMP evaluates gives_direct_check before the movecount/best_score gates — paid on every shallow quiet even when the prune cannot fire
finding.claim: In the LMP condition chain, the depth<4 check carve `(depth >= 4 || !board.gives_direct_check(mv))` is evaluated BEFORE `best_score > -(MATE_IN_MAX_PLY)`, before `FEAT_LMP`, and before the actual movecount test `move_count > lmp_limit` (which sits inside the block). Consequence: at depth 1-3 (the bulk of interior nodes), EVERY quiet non-promo move at every ply>0 non-check node calls gives_direct_check — including the first counted move (where best_score = -INFINITY makes pruning impossible) and all moves under the LMP limit. gives_direct_check (board.rs:564-638) does piece/king lookups, occupancy surgery, and up to two sliding-attack computations for slider movers or from-square/king alignment. Additionally, when the move survives LMP, the futility block may call gives_direct_check AGAIN for the same move at 4204 — a duplicate computation at depth<4. Coda's own futility block gets the ordering right (check test last, after `futility_value <= alpha`), matching Reckless; and no reference engine has a per-move board query in its LMP gate at all (SF/Berserk/Obsidian/Alexandria LMP is a bare count test) — the carve itself is Coda-unique, possibly a tested tunable choice, but the free win is the evaluation order. The reorder is semantics-preserving: the carve only matters when move_count > lmp_limit, so hoisting it inside that branch changes no prune decision (node-count identical).
finding.evidence: search.rs:3985-3993: `if ply > 0 && !in_check && depth >= 1 && depth <= tp(&LMP_DEPTH) && !is_cap && !is_promo && (depth >= 4 || !board.gives_direct_check(mv)) && best_score > -(MATE_IN_MAX_PLY) && beta < MATE_IN_MAX_PLY && FEAT_LMP... { let lmp_limit = (tp(&LMP_BASE) + depth * depth) / (2 - improving as i32); if move_count > lmp_limit { ... } }` — the expensive call precedes both the cheap gates and the count test. Duplicate call site: search.rs:4204 `if futility_value <= alpha && main_hist < 12000 && !board.gives_direct_check(mv)` (correct ordering: check test last). Contrast Reckless search.rs:730 `if !in_check && is_quiet && depth < 14 && futility_value <= alpha && !td.board.is_direct_check(mv)`; Stockfish search.cpp:1074 LMP is a bare count test `if (moveCount >= (3 + depth * depth) / (2 - improving)) mp.skip_quiet_moves();`; Berserk search.c:622, Obsidian search.cpp:1012, Alexandria search.cpp:706 likewise count-only.
finding.expected_impact: NPS ~0.2-0.8%, node-count identical (pure short-circuit reorder; gives_direct_check has no side effects). Ship-if-not-regression class ([-2,1]) or fold into another SPRT.
finding.suggested_change: Restructure to: outer gate = cheap conditions only (ply/depth/is_cap/best_score/beta/FEAT); inside: `if move_count > lmp_limit && (depth >= 4 || !board.gives_direct_check(mv)) { ... }`. Optionally memoize `gives_direct_check(mv)` in a per-move local (Option<bool>) shared between the LMP carve and the futility carve at depth<4.

finding.title: Main search lacks TT-bound refinement of the pruning eval (6/6 reference engines have it; Coda's own QS analog was +6.5 H1)
finding.claim: In negamax, the eval used for all static pruning (razoring, RFP, NMP eval gate, futility, hindsight) is `static_eval = corrected(scaled(raw_eval))` with NO refinement from the TT score bound. All 6 reference engines, after computing corrected static eval, replace/tighten a separate pruning-eval variable with the TT score whenever the stored bound direction agrees (LOWER and tt_score > eval, or UPPER and tt_score < eval), with NO depth requirement — so even a shallow searched bound sharpens every static-pruning decision. Coda's only bound-usage mechanism (window narrowing) requires tt_depth >= depth, so shallow-entry bound information is discarded entirely. Crucially, the consensus form keeps ss->staticEval UNREFINED for improving/corrhist and refines only the pruning variable — Coda would need a second variable (e.g. `pruning_eval`), leaving `static_eval` as-is for improving, corrhist update, and TT store (stores raw_eval). Caveat: a 2026-03-12 GoChess-era test of this idea was -77 Elo (experiments.md:812), but that implementation differed structurally: it added a depth gate (`entry.Depth >= depth-3`) the consensus form doesn't have, and per its own notes replaced the static eval wholesale (breaking improving/corrhist assumptions). The exact same consensus mechanism applied to the QS stand-pat was tested on Coda proper and scored +6.5 H1 (experiments.md:3823, fix-qs-tt-stand-pat: 'Every top engine does this'). The negamax analog is the missing half.

BOUND_LOWER : BOUND_UPPER))) eval = ttData.value;` (ss->staticEval stays unrefined); Reckless search.rs:422-441 `estimated_score = tt_score` when `Bound::Upper => tt_score < eval, Bound::Lower => tt_score > eval`; Obsidian search.cpp:836-837; Berserk search.c:476-477; PlentyChess search.cpp:752-753; Alexandria search.cpp:507-509. finding.title: Quiet futility runs AFTER SEE-quiet pruning — 5/6 references run cheap futility before the expensive SEE call
finding.claim: Coda's in-loop order for quiets is: LMP (3985) -> SEE-quiet (4028) -> singular-ext block -> futility (4188). SEE is the most expensive per-move prune (full exchange evaluation incl. the pinned-mask setup at see.rs:77-101); futility is one addition + comparison. The cost is compounded by the prunes' differing scope: SEE prune is a per-move `continue` while futility is TERMINAL (sets skip_quiets + picker.skip_remaining_quiets()) — so at a futile node (static_eval far below alpha, one of the most frequent prune situations), the loop keeps drawing quiets and re-running see_ge until one survives SEE and finally reaches the futility block that would have terminated ALL remaining quiets. 5 of 6 references order quiet futility before quiet SEE pruning (Stockfish, Reckless, Berserk, PlentyChess, Alexandria); only Obsidian puts SEE first. Both prunes' inputs (lmr_d at 4019, static_eval, hist) are available before either block, so swapping is a near-pure reorder; semantics shift only in that skip_quiets fires one-or-two moves earlier at futile nodes (strictly less work, near-identical tree). The singular-extension block between them is tt_move-only and unaffected by the swap.
finding.evidence: Coda: SEE-quiet at search.rs:4028-4039 (`let see_quiet_threshold = -tp(&SEE_QUIET_MULT) * lmr_d * lmr_d; if !see_ge(board, mv, see_quiet_threshold) { info.stats.see_prunes += 1; continue; }`) precedes futility at 4188-4209 (`let futility_value = static_eval + tp(&FUT_BASE) + lmr_d * tp(&FUT_PER_DEPTH) + hist_adj + threats_adj; if futility_value <= alpha ... { skip_quiets = true; picker.skip_remaining_quiets(); continue; }`). References (quiet path order): Stockfish search.cpp:1123 futility (`if (!ss->inCheck && lmrDepth < 13 && futilityValue <= alpha)`) before 1134 SEE (`if (!pos.see_ge(move, -25 * lmrDepth * lmrDepth))`); Reckless search.rs:730-736 FP before 754-763 SEE; Berserk search.c:633-634 FP before 636 SEE; PlentyChess search.cpp:963-973 FP before 1001-1003 SEE; Alexandria search.cpp:710-720 FP before 727-730 SEE. Exception: Obsidian search.cpp:1001-1004 SEE before 1017-1023 FP.
finding.expected_impact: NPS gain ~0.5-1.5% at shallow depths plus minor pruning-shape improvement (earlier node-wide quiet cutoff); small bench change, expected Elo-neutral-to-positive. [0,3] SPRT, or bundle with the lmr_d-history change (same code region).
finding.suggested_change: Move the quiet futility block (4186-4210) above the SEE-quiet block (4026-4040), keeping the shared lmr_d computation (4016-4024) before both.

verdict.prior_experiments: #2283 lmp/first-order (2026-06-25): reordered LMP ahead of SEE-quiet + futility, H1 +0.6 merged (399eb55) — same audit documented the SEE-quiet→futility order but only moved LMP. #2291 LMP-cluster retune post-reorder: flat, values only. #2072 quiet-see-hist: H0, different lever (history in SEE margin). No experiment has ever tested futility-before-SEE-quiet ordering.

The SEE cost claim is real: for quiets at shallow lmr_d the see_ge early-outs don't fire (pawn early-true only at lmr_d>=2, minors >=5), so the full pinned-mask loop (see.rs:77-101) runs where futility fires. Priority medium not high: no bug, bounded tiny NPS win, one top-3 engine (Obsidian) does the opposite, and the analog LMP reorder only bought +0.6.

finding.title: SEE-capture prune and BNFP re-run see_ge on captures whose result the picker's good/bad split already determines
finding.claim: The picker partitions captures by `see_ge(m, -capt_hist/18)` (movepicker.rs:533-534). The search then re-runs a full see_ge on the SAME move twice more: (1) SEE-cap prune calls `see_ge(mv, -cap_margin)` with cap_margin = max(0, depth*96 + cap_ch*11/1024). By SEE monotonicity (test see.rs:502), a good-stage capture with capt_hist <= ~2141*depth (i.e. capt_hist/18 <= cap_margin — the overwhelming majority) provably passes, so the call is dead work; (2) BNFP calls `see_ge(mv, 0)` whose result is also implied by the stage for capt_hist of the convenient sign (bad-stage + capt_hist>=0 => SEE<0; good-stage + capt_hist<=0 => SEE>=0). The wasted calls are not cheap: when the fast early-outs at see.rs:42-53 don't resolve (e.g. NxP with defender), see_ge builds BOTH pinned-piece masks (see.rs:77-101, ~4 sliding-attack scans + between() loops) before its swap loop. Every non-TT good capture at depth<=8 with ply>0 pays call (1); every eval-futile bad capture at depth<=9 pays both (1) and (2). Reckless avoids this class entirely by gating its BNFP on `move_picker.stage() == Stage::BadNoisy` instead of calling SEE (Reckless search.rs:745).
finding.evidence: search.rs:4009-4011 `let cap_ch = ...capt_hist_score_static(...); let cap_margin = (depth * tp(&SEE_CAP_MULT) + cap_ch * tp(&SEE_CAP_HIST) / 1024).max(0); if !see_ge(board, mv, -cap_margin)`; search.rs:4221 `&& !see_ge(board, mv, 0)`; movepicker.rs:533-534 `let see_threshold = -capt_hist / 18; if !see_ge(board, m, see_threshold)` (good/bad split). Derivation: good => SEE >= -capt_hist/18; prune needs SEE < -cap_margin, impossible unless capt_hist > 18*cap_margin ~= 2141*depth.
finding.expected_impact: NPS ~0.5-1.5% at shallow depths (also removes a duplicate capt_hist table lookup already done at scoring). Bench-identical if implemented exactly (skip-only-when-provably-dead); Reckless-style stage gating is a small semantic change worth its own [0,3].
finding.suggested_change: Expose the current stage (or a came_from_bad_captures flag) from MovePicker. In the SEE-cap prune, short-circuit to 'no prune' when the move came from the good-captures stage and `cap_ch <= 18*cap_margin` (exact, cheap integer check). In BNFP, replace/short-circuit `!see_ge(mv,0)` using the stage: bad-stage with cap_ch>=0 => known SEE<0; good-stage with cap_ch<=0 => known SEE>=0; only call see_ge in the ambiguous remainder (or adopt Reckless's pure stage gate as a separate SPRT).

verdict.prior_experiments: 2026-03-12 "QS Skip Bad Captures (remove double SEE)" — same idea family (avoid double SEE for good captures), QS-only: -2 Elo at 1366 games, killed as strength-neutral, note reads "the NPS gain from one fewer SEE call per QS capture is negligible". Caveat: predates the 2026-06-23 pin-mask addition to see_ge (commit 67a3b24), which made see_ge materially more expensive, and was bundled with skipping bad captures entirely. Adjacent-but-different: #1942 bnfp-victim H0 +0.1 (BNFP victim term, closed), #2117 s2-see-cap-depth-raise H0 -1.1 (SEE_CAP_DEPTH ceiling calibrated). No prior test of main-search redundant-SEE elimination or Reckless-style BNFP stage gating.
verdict.reasoning: Mechanism confirmed line-by-line. Picker splits captures via see_ge(m, -capt_hist/18) (movepicker.rs:531-534); search then re-calls see_ge on the same move in the SEE-cap prune (search.rs:4008-4014, SEE_CAP_MULT=96/SEE_CAP_HIST=11/SEE_CAP_DEPTH=8 — reviewer's ~2141*depth threshold derivation is arithmetically correct) and in BNFP (search.rs:4221, see_ge(mv,0), BAD_NOISY_DEPTH=9). see_ge monotonicity is an explicitly tested invariant (see_ge_monotonicity test), so the stage-implication logic is sound. The expensive path is real: both pinned-piece masks are built unconditionally before the swap loop (see.rs:77-101) whenever the early-outs at see.rs:42-53 don't resolve; these masks were added 2026-06-23, AFTER the only prior test of this idea family. Reckless citation verified (search.rs:744 gates BNFP on move_picker.stage() == Stage::BadNoisy, no SEE call). Guards checked: prune requires !in_check (matches picker non-evasion path) and mv != tt_move (picker filters TT move), so all moves reaching the prunes did pass through the good/bad split — no neutralizing gate found. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) 'bench-identical if implemented exactly' is wrong as proposed — capture history drifts within a node (child-subtree beta cutoffs update info.history.capture at search.rs ~4767/4795 and ~3298 between picker generation and the prune's re-read), so the suggested re-read-based check cap_ch <= 18*cap_margin does not exactly reproduce the generation-time guarantee; exact skip requires the picker to expose the generation-time capt_hist/threshold per move (easy — it's embedded in the stored score). (2) 'Reckless avoids this class entirely' is true only for BNFP: Reckless's SEE pruning still calls see(mv, threshold) on every capture including good-stage ones, and Stockfish likewise (picker split movepick.cpp:237, search re-run search.cpp:1099) — so claim (1)'s redundancy is shared by the top-2 engines, meaning it is not a structural gap, purely an NPS micro-opt they tolerate, which caps expected impact (many good-stage calls also resolve in the cheap early-outs; the 0.5-1.5% NPS estimate is unverified and likely at the low end given the March in-family test measured 'negligible'). Verdict: confirmed as an NPS-opportunity with corrected details; the Reckless-style BNFP stage gate is an untested, cheap, consensus-sourced [0,3] side experiment. Not a bug; magnitude modest.

finding.title: TT bounds-narrowing mutates alpha/beta past each other when halfmove gate blocks the cutoff — search continues with an inverted window
finding.claim: At a zero-width node (beta - alpha_orig == 1), the fall-through 'narrowing' can only ever fully collapse the window: for LOWER, `tt_score > alpha` at ZW implies `tt_score >= beta`, so `alpha = tt_score` gives alpha >= beta; symmetrically for UPPER, `beta = tt_score` gives beta <= alpha. The collapse-return at line 3284 is gated on `halfmove_ok` (halfmove < 89, the P2 stale-TT protection), but the alpha/beta MUTATION at 3270-3282 is NOT. So at halfmove >= 89 with a deep-enough LOWER entry above beta (or UPPER below alpha), the node proceeds into the full move loop with alpha >= beta — an inverted window. Every child is then searched with an inverted window recursively (child gets (-beta, -alpha) which is also inverted), NMP is disabled (`beta - alpha == 1` false), futility/razoring compare against the inflated alpha, and the node finally TT-stores a full-depth bound derived from this degenerate search — re-stamping, at current generation and full depth, exactly the stale near-50mr bound P2 was added to distrust. The in-code comment ('Window-narrowing is still applied — it only biases the search', line 3188) shows the author believed narrowing was a benign bias; at ZW it is never a bias, always a collapse. Concrete trace: shuffling endgame, board.halfmove = 92, ZW node alpha=50/beta=51, TT entry {LOWER, depth >= current depth, tt_score=120}. halfmove_ok=false -> direct cutoff (3210) skipped; 3273 sets alpha=120; 3284 skipped (halfmove_ok false); move loop runs with (alpha=120, beta=51).
finding.evidence: search.rs:3190 `let halfmove_ok = (board.halfmove as i32) < tp(&TT_CUTOFF_HALFMOVE_MAX);` (default 89). search.rs:3271-3280 `TT_FLAG_LOWER => { if beta - alpha_orig == 1 && tt_score > alpha { alpha = tt_score; } } TT_FLAG_UPPER => { if beta - alpha_orig == 1 && tt_score < beta { beta = tt_score; } }` — no halfmove_ok. search.rs:3284 `if alpha >= beta && halfmove_ok { ... return ... }` — the only exit. Nothing between 3340 and the move loop restores alpha/beta. experiments.md (#628 P2) confirms the halfmove gate was extended 'to bounds-narrow collapse' — i.e. to the RETURN, leaving the mutation ungated. Verified in current checkout 2026-07-01.
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness — fires in precisely the 50-move-rule-adjacent endgames P2 was written to protect (halfmove 89-99, TT-heavy shuffle positions); degenerate subtrees plus full-depth TT re-poisoning of stale bounds; likely small overall Elo but real conversion-behavior fix
finding.suggested_change: Gate the narrowing block on halfmove_ok too (wrap the `match tt_entry.flag` at 3270 in `if halfmove_ok { ... }`), so when the halfmove gate rejects the TT score the node searches with its original window as intended.

verdict.prior_experiments: #628 P2 halfmove-gated TT cutoff (2026-04-22, +1.2 Elo H1, 13970g): "Extended existing halfmove < 90 gate to bounds-narrow collapse + near-miss + QS TT cutoff return paths" — gated the RETURNS only, leaving the alpha/beta mutation ungated, exactly as the finding claims. #1931 ttcut-bonus-lower-only (H0 -1.6): different issue (history bonus at the collapse site, not window gating). No prior experiment has gated the narrowing mutation itself; not in Suspects/Retry sections.
verdict.reasoning: Mechanism verified line by line in src/search.rs (fn negamax). (1) Narrowing (actual lines 3256-3268, not 3270-3282 as cited — reviewer's line numbers are off by ~14 but all quoted code matches verbatim) fires only at ZW (`beta - alpha_orig == 1`), and alpha == alpha_orig there (MDP/cuckoo/TB mutations happen before alpha_orig capture at 3146). At ZW, LOWER with tt_score > alpha implies tt_score >= beta, so alpha = tt_score always fully collapses the window; UPPER symmetric. The in-code comment "it only biases the search" is wrong for the only case narrowing applies. (2) halfmove_ok (line 3176, TT_CUTOFF_HALFMOVE_MAX default 89) gates the direct cutoff (3197), collapse return (3270), and near-miss (3331) but NOT the mutation; when halfmove_ok is true the collapse-return block always returns (3322/3325), so the leak exists only at halfmove >= 89. Grep confirms nothing restores alpha/beta between 3268 and the move loop. (3) Reachable: the 50mr draw return at 2972 only catches halfmove >= 100, so 89-99 nodes reach the TT block; conditions (ply>0, no excluded move, tt_depth >= depth, ZW, collapsing bound) are routine in TT-heavy shuffle endgames. (4) Downstream claims verified: children get inverted (-beta,-alpha); NMP gated on beta-alpha==1 (3651) is disabled; the node beta-cutoffs on eval-quality child returns and TT-stores at full depth/current generation, defeating P2's purpose. (5) reference engines return directly on bound match and never mutate alpha/beta from TT — the mutating-narrowing construct is Coda-specific, so the bug is Coda's own, not a mis-ported consensus pattern. (6) QS analog (5044-5058) is returns-only, clean. Severity: real correctness bug with a trivial fix (wrap the match in `if halfmove_ok`), but the regime is narrow and the degenerate search returns eval-derived (not random) scores, so expected Elo is small — priority medium rather than high; test as [-2,1] correctness fix per bug-fix bounds policy.

finding.title: TT prefetch is a compile-time no-op on aarch64 — every info.tt.prefetch() call site does nothing on a first-class platform
finding.claim: TT::prefetch only emits a prefetch under `#[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]`; on aarch64 the function computes the bucket pointer and discards it. The search calls prefetch at ~8 sites (node entry, post-make_move, QS, NMP, ProbCut) specifically to hide TT-bucket miss latency, and CLAUDE.md lists 'TT prefetch' as a load-bearing optimization. On Apple M-series / Graviton with a large Hash, every probe is a cold DRAM hit with no overlap. The threats.rs SIMD prefetches (1910, 2248) have the same x86-only shape, so the whole prefetch strategy is absent on ARM.
finding.evidence: tt.rs:512-519: `pub fn prefetch(&self, hash: u64) { let idx = ...; let ptr = ...; #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")] unsafe { std::arch::x86_64::_mm_prefetch(ptr as *const i8, _MM_HINT_T0); } }` — no aarch64 arm; `grep -rn prefetch src/` shows only x86_64 intrinsics across the codebase. CLAUDE.md: 'aarch64 (first-class, since 2026-04-25)'.
finding.expected_impact: quality/NPS on ARM only (dev boxes / any ARM deployment); zero effect on OB/lichess x86. Cheap, contained change
finding.suggested_change: Add an aarch64 arm using inline asm: `#[cfg(target_arch = "aarch64")] unsafe { core::arch::asm!("prfm pldl1keep, [{0}]", in(reg) ptr, options(nostack, preserves_flags)); }` (same for the threats.rs prefetch helpers). Verify with an M-series bench NPS A/B on an uncontended box.

verdict.prior_experiments: No prior test of aarch64 TT prefetch found (novelty holds for the TT half). Related prefetch history is cautionary though: #719 experiment/prefetch-threat-deltas −4.4 H0, #721 tier-1 retry −8.1 H0 (2026-04); #932 extra search-side prefetch −2 ±5 verified-not-Elo, closed (2026-05-04, cache-hygiene leg: "textbook optimizations that should obviously help repeatedly H0'd"); 2026-06-14 "NNUE prefetch thread CLOSED negative: mechanism real, lever doesn't convert" — FT-side neutral, "Every threat-side prefetch REGRESSES", early make_move-time prefetch worst (−8.6). #764 fix/aarch64-tt-tbcache-ordering (ARM correctness, merged) shows ARM-parity work is accepted policy but was correctness, not NPS. #1947 perf-node-entry H0 confirms the x86 TT prefetch spacing is load-bearing (prefetch at node entry, compute, then probe).
verdict.reasoning: Code claim verified line by line: tt.rs:512-519 emits a prefetch only under #[cfg(target_arch = "x86_64")]; there is no aarch64 arm anywhere in the codebase (grep confirms only x86_64 intrinsics), and all 7 search.rs prefetch call sites (3012, 3677, 3831, 4250, 4994, 5150, 5362) are no-ops on ARM. No neutralizing guard exists elsewhere. Minor correction: the "computes the bucket pointer and discards it" cost is illusory — LLVM dead-code-eliminates it — so it's a silent no-op, not overhead. The suggested inline-asm fix (prfm pldl1keep) is the right approach on stable Rust since std::arch::aarch64::_prefetch is unstable. TWO corrections that cut the finding's scope, though: (1) The threats.rs extension (lines 1910, 2248) should be DROPPED — those prefetches live inside x86-only SIMD kernels (ARM uses separate NEON kernels), and the experiments record shows threat-side prefetch REGRESSES even on x86 (#719 −4.4 H0, #721 −8.1 H0, and the 2026-06-14 prefetch-ladder closure). Porting them to ARM would replicate a known-negative lever. (2) Impact is bounded lower than the finding implies: per CLAUDE.md, ALL rating-bearing deployments (OB fleet, lichess codabot, CCRL, all SPRT gating) are x86_64; ARM is dev boxes (MacBook M5) and hypothetical Graviton. It also cannot be SPRT-gated on the x86 OB fleet — validation is a local M-series uncontended NPS A/B only (per the NPS-measurement discipline note). The mechanism itself is plausibly real for the TT half — TT access is hash-random so no HW prefetcher helps, and #1947 independently confirmed the node-entry prefetch spacing pays for itself on x86 — so a cheap, contained aarch64 arm for TT::prefetch only is a legitimate small NPS experiment. Priority low: ARM-only NPS with no rating-bearing ARM deployment today, prefetch levers have a poor conversion record here, and the win is likely single-digit % NPS at best.

finding.title: TT cutoff depth condition is symmetric in bound direction; 4/6 references demand one EXTRA ply for fail-high cutoffs and give fail-low a free 1-ply grace (no margin)
finding.claim: Coda gates the TT cutoff on `tt_depth >= depth` identically for both bound directions, with a separate near-miss branch accepting depth-1 entries in BOTH directions behind an 80cp margin. The consensus shape in 4 of 6 references is asymmetric by bound direction: fail-high (score >= beta) cutoffs require tt_depth >= depth+1, while fail-low cutoffs are accepted at tt_depth >= depth — equivalently, fail-low entries get a free one-ply grace with NO margin, and fail-high entries need extra depth. Relative to that consensus Coda is simultaneously MORE permissive on the risky direction (a depth-1 LOWER entry 80cp above beta cuts a node SF would require depth+1 for — two plies of slack difference) and LESS permissive on the safe direction (fail-low at depth-1 pays an 80cp toll that SF/Reckless/Obsidian/Plenty grant free). Mechanism: fail-high TT cutoffs prune the whole node (highest risk of stale-bound damage), fail-low cutoffs only confirm an all-node. The near-miss feature itself is SPRT-tested (CLAUDE.md), but the direction asymmetry — the structural part — has apparently never been ported.
finding.evidence: Coda search.rs:3191 `if tt_depth >= depth && FEAT_TT_CUTOFF...` (both directions), near-miss 3341-3349 `tt_depth >= depth - 1 ... margin = 80; if LOWER && tt_score - margin >= beta return tt_score - margin; if UPPER && tt_score + margin <= alpha return tt_score + margin`. References with the asymmetry: Stockfish search.cpp:780 `ttData.depth > depth - (ttData.value <= beta)`; Reckless search.rs:341 `tt_depth > depth - (tt_score < beta) as i32`; Obsidian search.cpp:746 `ttDepth >= depth + (ttScore >= beta)`; PlentyChess search.cpp:678 `ttDepth >= depth - ttCutOffset + ttCutFailHighMargin * (ttValue >= beta)`. Symmetric like Coda: Alexandria search.cpp:473, Berserk search.c:432. 4 vs 2 among the reference set, including the top 3.
finding.expected_impact: +0-2 Elo guess
finding.suggested_change: Test the consensus asymmetry: change the main gate to `tt_depth > depth - (tt_score < beta) as i32` and restrict (or re-tune) the 80cp near-miss to the fail-high direction only, since fail-low's grace becomes free. Retune-on-branch candidate (tree-shape change); SPRT [0,3].

Adjacent (tested, different levers): TT near-miss merged 2026-03 (margin 64->80 MERGED; 96 REJECTED twice, listed as +1.6 retry-candidate; 112 REJECTED; ablation 'No TT Near-miss -23/-26 Important'); #628 halfmove-gated TT cutoff +1.2 H1; #149 fix-tt-cutoff-nodetype (Alexandria cut_node guard) +2.4 H1; #2124 atlas/tt-cutoff-deep-relax (port SF's depth>5 relaxation of the cut_node guard) H0 -0.2 DROPPED; #1931 ttcut-bonus-lower-only H0; #672 tt-cutoff-malus-symmetry H0 -1.7.

finding.title: All three qsearch TT stores hardcode tt_pv=false — sticky PV flag is erased on same-key overwrites and never set by PV qsearch nodes
finding.claim: QS stores pass a literal `false` for the is_pv/tt_pv argument at all three store sites. tt.rs store() packs the caller's is_pv verbatim on same-key updates (no OR with the slot's existing bit), and same-key overwrite is unconditional when `gen != slot_gen` (tt.rs:478). So at the start of every new search, the first QS visit to a position holding a previous search's tt_pv=true entry erases the sticky PV marker (negamax preserves it because it passes the probed-and-ORed `tt_pv` local; QS does not). Additionally, PV qsearch nodes (beta-alpha>1) never mark their positions PV at all. tt_pv feeds the LMR -1 reduction, the RFP tt_pv skip, and SE margins; the TT-PV flag was worth +4.5 raw / +8.5 with retune when introduced (experiments.md #160), so silently stripping it from PV leaf regions is a measurable leak. SF's qsearch computes `pvHit = ttHit && tte->is_pv()` and stores `PvNode || pvHit`; Coda's QS already computes `qs_is_pv` and has `tt_entry.tt_pv` in scope but uses neither for the store.
finding.evidence: search.rs:5199 `info.tt.store(board.hash, -1, store_score, flag, best_move, -INFINITY, false);` (evasion path); 5268-5269 `info.tt.store(board.hash, -1, score_to_tt(best_score, ply), TT_FLAG_LOWER, NO_MOVE, raw_stand_pat, false);` (stand-pat fail-high); 5403 `info.tt.store(board.hash, -1, store_score, flag, best_move, raw_stand_pat, false);` (capture loop). tt.rs:476-489 same-key path: `if depth > slot_depth - 3 || gen != slot_gen || flag_is_exact { ... pack_data(effective_move, flag, static_eval, score, depth, gen, is_pv) ... }` — is_pv taken from caller, prior slot's pv bit discarded. finding.title: best_move recorded without the score>alpha gate, so fail-low (UPPER) stores overwrite the TT move with the 'least-bad' move — all 6 references gate on alpha and preserve the prior move
finding.claim: Coda assigns `best_move = mv` whenever `score > best_score` (search.rs:4628; same shape in QS at 5171 and 5381), so on a fail-low node best_move is the arbitrary least-bad move of a search where every move failed. The final store then writes this move into the TT under an UPPER bound, and — because best_move is never NO_MOVE in main negamax — the move-preservation logic in tt.rs:480-484 ('all-node stores with NO_MOVE must not erase a move... all 5 reference engines implement this') is dead code for negamax stores: a shallower fail-low revisit actively REPLACES a deeper iteration's proven cutoff move. All 6 reference engines assign bestMove only inside `score > alpha`, so their fail-low stores pass a null move and their TT keeps the previous move (SF tt.cpp:97-98 `if (m || uint16_t(k) != key16) move16 = m;`, Reckless transposition.rs:205-207 `if !(entry.key == key && mv.is_null()) { entry.mv = mv; }`). Downstream, a planted UPPER tt_move also suppresses IIR (gate `tt_move == NO_MOVE`), where references would have reduced. finding.title: TT dampening, near-miss, and fail-high blending gate on mate-only bounds — TB-band scores pass and get arithmetically mangled
finding.claim: The guards `tt_score > -(MATE_IN_MAX_PLY) && tt_score < MATE_IN_MAX_PLY` (MATE_IN_MAX_PLY = 28872) do not exclude Syzygy scores: a definite TB win is `TB_WIN - ply` = 28800 - ply < 28872, so it passes every one of these 'non-decisive' gates. Consequences: (a) TT dampening returns `(w*(TB_WIN-ply) + beta)/(w+1)` — e.g. w=3, beta=100 gives ~21618, a fabricated huge score that has left the TB band (>28600 threshold) so it is never ply-adjusted again by score_to_tt, destroying the distance-to-win encoding that drives TB conversion; (b) near-miss returns `tt_score - 80` = 28720-ply, still inside the score_to_tt band, so the parent's store ply-adjusts an already-margin-shifted TB score; (c) fail-high blending and both QS beta-blends similarly average TB scores with beta. The repo added `is_decisive()` (tt.rs:605, TB_WIN-200) in the 2026-06-11 audit T2.3 explicitly because 'the widespread |s| < MATE_IN_MAX_PLY mate guards admit TB scores', and it is used at the multicut return and ProbCut return — but these TT-score shaping sites were not converted. Only fires with SyzygyPath set (lichess/CCRL deployment, not OB), which is why SPRT never catches it.
finding.evidence: search.rs:3331-3336 `if beta - alpha_orig == 1 && tt_entry.flag == TT_FLAG_LOWER && tt_score > -(MATE_IN_MAX_PLY) && tt_score < MATE_IN_MAX_PLY { let w = tp(&TT_DAMP_TT_WEIGHT); return (w * tt_score + beta) / (w + 1); }`; 3341-3349 near-miss same bounds then `return tt_score - margin;`; 4926 `return (best_score * depth + beta) / (depth + tp(&FH_BLEND_OFFSET)).max(1);` behind the same mate-only bounds. tt.rs:599-607: `is_decisive` doc: 'use this where TB scores must also be excluded (SF/Reckless/Stormphrax is_decisive; 2026-06-11 audit T2.3)'. TB_WIN band: tt.rs:578, TB scores set in negamax TB probe as `TB_WIN - ply`.
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness for TB-enabled deployment (lichess/CCRL): prevents TB-win distance corruption and shuffle-prone conversion in tablebase endgames; ~0 on OB (no TB on fleet)

finding.title: Fail-high blending applied AFTER the TT store: TT keeps the raw inflated LOWER bound while the parent receives the dampened score (SF, the feature's source, blends before the write)
finding.claim: Coda stores `store_score = score_to_tt(best_score, ply)` and only afterwards applies fail-high blending `(best_score * depth + beta) / (depth + OFFSET)` at 4926 to the RETURN value. Stockfish — the only reference engine with this feature — mutates bestValue with the blend (search.cpp:1427-1428) BEFORE the ttWriter.write at 1485-1490, so its TT bound is the dampened value. Consequence of Coda's ordering: the search path that actually ran gets the dampened score, but every future TT hit on that entry (direct cutoff returns tt_score raw; the TT_DAMP dampening only fires on the node-type-mismatch path) returns the undampened, inflated fail-high value — the same position yields a systematically higher score via TT replay than via search, re-introducing exactly the score inflation the blend was SPRT'd in to remove, and doing so inconsistently across paths (which also feeds aspiration/TM score-trend logic noisier values on TT-warm iterations).
finding.evidence: Coda search.rs:4848-4851 `let store_score = score_to_tt(best_score, ply); ... info.tt.store(board.hash, depth, store_score, flag, best_move, raw_eval, tt_pv);` then 4918-4926 `if best_score >= beta && beta - alpha_orig == 1 && depth >= tp10(&FH_BLEND_DEPTH_10X) ... return (best_score * depth + beta) / (depth + tp(&FH_BLEND_OFFSET)).max(1);`. Stockfish search.cpp:1427-1428 `if (bestValue >= beta && !is_decisive(bestValue) && !is_decisive(alpha)) bestValue = (bestValue * depth + beta) / (depth + 1);` occurs before search.cpp:1485-1490 `ttWriter.write(posKey, value_to_tt(bestValue, ss->ply), ...)`. No other reference engine has FH blending (grep for '* depth + beta' empty in Reckless/Obsidian/Plenty/Alexandria/Berserk), so SF's before-store placement is the only prior art.
finding.expected_impact: +0-2 Elo guess / consistency fix
finding.suggested_change: Move the blend before the TT store (blend best_score into a local, store and return the blended value, keeping the excluded_move and mate guards), matching SF. Note the SE-verification skip must keep receiving the raw score — compute the blend into the stored/returned value only when excluded_move is NO_MOVE, which the current gate already ensures. SPRT [0,3] or [-1.5,1.5].

finding.title: 50-move-rule draw return lacks the checkmate exception — all 6 reference engines verify the side to move is not mated before returning the rule-50 draw
finding.claim: Both negamax and qsearch return draw_score=0 unconditionally when `board.halfmove >= 100`. Under FIDE rules (and every adjudicator, including cutechess/lichess), checkmate takes precedence: if the move that made the halfmove clock reach 100 delivered mate, the game is a win/loss, not a draw. Trace: opponent plays a quiet checkmating move that is the 100th halfmove → Coda's child node enters negamax with halfmove==100, in check, zero legal moves → returns 0 at line 2973 instead of `-MATE_SCORE + ply` (checkmate detection at 4816-4819 is unreachable because the draw return fires first; checkers are only computed later at 3354) → the parent scores the mating line as a draw. Dangerous both ways: when losing near the 50-move boundary Coda can 'escape' into a line it scores 0 that the arbiter scores as Coda being checkmated; when winning it avoids a mate that lands exactly at halfmove 100 because it reads as a draw. All six reference engines gate the rule-50 draw on 'not in check, or at least one legal move exists'; the check is free in practice because it only runs when halfmove>=100.
finding.evidence: Coda negamax lines 2970-2974: `if ply > 0 { let draw_score: i32 = 0; if board.halfmove >= 100 { return draw_score; }` — no checkers/legal-move test; same in quiescence (4970-4972). Stockfish position.cpp:1523: `if (st->rule50 > 99 && (!checkers() || MoveList<LEGAL>(*this).size())) return true;`. Reckless board.rs:283-285: `self.halfmove_clock() >= 100 && (!self.in_check() || self.has_legal_moves())`. Obsidian position.cpp:112-118: `if (halfMoveClock < 100) return false; if (!checkers) return true;` then generates evasions. Berserk board.c:555-562: `if (board->fmr > 99) { if (board->checkers) { RootMoves(moves, board); return moves->count > 0; } ...}`. PlentyChess search.cpp:408-414 and Alexandria search.cpp:46-56: same pattern with explicit 'might be checkmate' comments. 6/6 on the other side.
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness; rare edge case (~0-0.5 Elo) but the failure mode is a full point, and the fix is cheap and consensus-backed
finding.suggested_change: Gate the halfmove>=100 draw return on `checkers == 0 || at least one legal move exists` in both negamax and quiescence (compute checkers lazily only when halfmove>=100). SPRT [-2,1] as a correctness fix.

finding.title: xray-SE margin: code direction is the opposite of the documented mechanism (widening singular_beta margin gives FEWER extensions on xray TT moves, not more), and SPSA range [0,400] cannot explore the intended sign
finding.claim: Both the inline comment and the tunables comment claim the xray bonus makes singularity EASIER ('widen margin → easier singular → more extensions on tactical discoveries'), but the code does the opposite. `singular_beta = tt_score_local - depth - xray_bonus` LOWERS singular_beta for xray-blocker TT moves. The extension condition is `singular_score < singular_beta` (all alternatives strictly below the bar): lowering the bar makes it HARDER for the exclusion search to stay under it, so the TT move is judged singular LESS often → fewer +1/+2 extensions; the fall-through `singular_score >= singular_beta` branches (negative extensions at ~4135-4148, multicut) fire MORE often. Concrete trace: tt_score=100, depth=10, best alternative=85. Without bonus: singular_beta=90, 85<90 → singular → +1 ext. With bonus 5 (tp10(46)=5): singular_beta=85, 85>=85 → NOT singular → falls into negative-ext/reduce path. So xray TT moves — the 'tactically significant discoveries' the feature says it wants to search deeper — are extended less and reduced more. The feature as coded DID pass SPRT (#604 se-xray-blocker H1 +1.1, 25,934g, experiments.md:5432), so the shipped behavior is empirically fine at its tiny 5cp magnitude — the docs describe an inverted mechanism. This matters beyond hygiene: (a) SPSA's range is [0, 400] (`SE_XRAY_BLOCKER_MARGIN_10X, 46, 0, 400`), so the tuner can never test the sign the stated intent implies (`+ xray_bonus` on singular_beta), and (b) a future maintainer reading the comment could 'fix' the formula in the wrong direction on a feature that was validated as-is.
finding.expected_impact: quality (correct a mis-documented shipped mechanism; prevents a wrong-direction 'fix') plus a cheap probe: a [-1.5,1.5] or [0,3] test of the opposite sign (`tt_score - depth + xray_bonus`), which SPSA structurally cannot reach today
finding.suggested_change: Rewrite both comments to state the actual mechanism (bonus widens the margin → STRICTER singularity → fewer positive extensions / more negative extensions and multicut on xray-blocker TT moves — empirically +1.1 in #604). Optionally run one cheap SPRT with the sign flipped to test the originally-intended direction, since the SPSA range floor of 0 has never allowed it.

verdict.prior_experiments: #604 experiment/se-xray-blocker — H1 +1.1 Elo, 25,934g (experiments.md:5432-5435): the feature AS CODED passed SPRT. Tune #816 (2026-04-27): SE_XRAY_BLOCKER eff 4→3. Tune #1915 (2026-06-11, LTC Hash=256): SE_XRAY_BLOCKER_MARGIN 33→42 (stored _10X) — SPSA actively pushes the value UP, away from the 0 floor. Also relevant: early singular-margin experiment (experiments.md ~line 1250) states the correct direction convention ('tighten margin → more moves singular → more extensions'), contradicting the shipped comments. No prior test of the opposite sign (+xray_bonus / negative margin) exists — range floor has always been 0. No prior entry notes the comment inversion.
verdict.reasoning: Verified line-by-line on current main. singular_beta = tt_score_local - depth - xray_bonus (search.rs:4082); extension gate singular_score < singular_beta (4112). Subtracting the bonus LOWERS the bar; the exclusion search's alternatives reach a lower bar more easily (fail high at window (singular_beta-1, singular_beta)) → TT move judged singular LESS often → fewer +1/+2 extensions, and the negative-ext branches (4140-4152) fire more often. tp10(46)=(46+5)/10=5, so the reviewer's concrete trace (tt=100, d=10, alt=85: 85<90 singular without bonus; 85>=85 not singular with bonus) is exact. Both comments (search.rs:4076-4078 inline, 408-412 tunables) state the inverted causal chain 'widen margin → easier singular → more extensions'. Direction convention independently confirmed two ways: (1) Stockfish search.cpp:1147 comment 'higher singularBeta (i.e closer to ttValue) and lower extension margins scale well'; (2) Coda's own experiments.md ~1250: 'Tighten singular extension margin from ttScore-depth*3 to depth*2. More moves become singular → more extensions.' So the shipped comments are definitively inverted vs both SF and Coda's own historical understanding. One partial correction: 'multicut fires more often' is only half-right — multicut (4093) needs singular_score >= singular_beta AND singular_beta >= beta; lowering singular_beta eases the first but hardens the second, so net multicut effect is ambiguous (negative-ext claim is fully correct). The SPSA-range point is structurally true (floor 0 can never express the +xray_bonus sign), BUT the suggested sign-flip probe is weakly motivated: SPSA has had the 0 floor available across multiple tunes and never pins there — it holds eff 3-5 and INCREASED the value at LTC (#1915: 33→42), i.e., the gradient near zero points toward the coded strict direction, making the opposite sign a likely loser. Net: real, new, correctly-diagnosed misdocumentation of a shipped +1.1-validated mechanism; the actionable fix is rewriting the two comments (prevents a future wrong-direction 'fix' of a validated feature); the optional sign-flip SPRT is marginal. Priority low because the confirmed defect is documentation-only (zero Elo) and the experiment component is contra-indicated by SPSA evidence.

finding.title: LMR is skipped entirely at in-check nodes (both quiet and capture paths)
finding.claim: Coda gates both LMR blocks on `!in_check` (node in check), so check-evasion moves are NEVER reduced — every evasion at every depth is searched at full depth. None of the 6 reference engines has any in-check condition on their LMR entry gate; they reduce evasions with the normal table (the small evasion move counts naturally keep reductions modest). The gate dates unchanged to the original translation (2ff2b77), is absent from the 2026-06-23 LMR audit (neither in findings L1-L9 nor in its 'confirmed correct' list), and experiments.md has no test of it (the '!givesCheck LMR skip is well-calibrated' note at experiments.md:942 is about moves that GIVE check, a different thing). Mechanism: at deep in-check nodes with 3+ evasions (Coda's table is zero below moves>=3, which bounds but does not eliminate the effect), Coda burns full-depth searches on late evasions that peers reduce by 1-2, bloating forcing/king-hunt subtrees.

finding.expected_impact: +0-2 Elo guess (node savings in forcing lines); risk that the gate is a calibrated carve — prior 'asymmetric gate' audit claims have H0'd, though those were depth-vs-lmrDepth gates, not whole-feature carves

finding.title: Next-iteration time estimate uses a stale `elapsed` snapshot taken before the forced-move verification search
finding.claim: TM audit A4 fixed the soft-budget check to re-read the clock (`elapsed_now` at 2833: 'the iteration-top elapsed snapshot predates the info-line print and any forced-move verification (50-150ms)'), but the next-iteration hard-window estimate three lines later still uses the STALE `elapsed` from line 2464 (taken before PV extraction, the info print, stability tracking, and the forced-move verification search which the code itself documents as costing 50-150ms). `(effective_hard - elapsed) < 2 * iter_elapsed` therefore overestimates the remaining hard budget by exactly the verification cost on the one iteration per search where the detector fires — allowing an unaffordable iteration to start, which then burns until the in-search hard-limit stop fires mid-iteration (wasted nodes, partial iteration discarded).
finding.evidence: Line 2464: `let elapsed = info.start_time.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;` (before PV print at 2545 and forced-move verification at 2659-2661). Line 2833: `let elapsed_now = info.start_time.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;` used only for the soft check at 2835. Lines 2850-2854: `if effective_hard > 0 { let iter_elapsed = iter_start.elapsed()...; if elapsed > 0 && effective_hard > elapsed && (effective_hard - elapsed) < 2 * iter_elapsed { break; } }` — uses the stale `elapsed`.
finding.expected_impact: quality / minor TM correctness; at most one wasted partial iteration per search, on searches where the forced-move detector fires near the budget boundary. One-line fix.
finding.suggested_change: Use `elapsed_now` (already computed at 2833) in the 2850-2854 check instead of the iteration-top `elapsed`.

verdict.reasoning: Textually verified: src/search.rs:2852 uses the iteration-top `elapsed` (line 2464, taken before PV extraction, info print, and the 50-150ms forced-move verification at 2659-2661) while the A4 fix's `elapsed_now` (line 2833) is used only for the soft check at 2835. No reassignment of `elapsed` in between; the A4 comment (2828-2832) names exactly this staleness, so the fix was applied to one of two consumers. The core mechanism survives, but two details need correcting: (1) the verification runs on EVERY iteration with depth>=8 while tm_forced_state==None (gate at 2636), not once per search — so the staleness recurs on most iterations of a normal search; (2) on the iteration where the detector actually FIRES, iter_elapsed (read at 2851, includes verification cost V) inflates the RHS by 2V while stale elapsed inflates the LHS by only V, and the next iteration pays no V — so the check is net OVER-conservative there, opposite of the reviewer's story. The genuinely under-conservative case is the common non-firing verification iterations, where the RHS fairly estimates the next iteration (which will pay V again) and the stale LHS grants ~50-150ms of unwarranted slack. Impact is bounded as claimed: the in-search hard stop and abs_deadline still fire, so worst case is one wasted partial iteration near the hard boundary — no forfeit risk. One-line fix (use elapsed_now), bench-neutral, [-2,1]/hygiene class, natural to bundle with the next TM hygiene pass (same class as #1949).

finding.claim: At ply >= MAX_PLY negamax returns apply_halfmove_scale(info.eval(board), ...) unconditionally, and quiescence does the same at qs_depth >= 32 — both paths are reachable while in check (QS evasion chains recurse with qs_depth+1). finding.title: No TT-score refinement of eval at negamax node entry (all 6 reference engines have it; Coda only does it in qsearch)
finding.claim: Coda computes static_eval (raw -> halfmove-scaled -> corrhist-corrected) and feeds it directly into razoring, RFP, NMP, futility, BNFP and the ProbCut SEE threshold. finding.title: Qsearch checkmate scores at ply > MAX_PLY fall below the mate-recognition band into the TB score range
finding.claim: Negamax guards ply at MAX_PLY (2985), but quiescence has only a qs_depth cap (4986: `if qs_depth >= 32`), so QS chains entered from negamax at ply up to 127 can recurse to ply ~159. The evasion checkmate return at 5169 (`return -MATE_SCORE + ply;`) then produces scores with |score| as low as MATE_SCORE-159 = 28841, which is BELOW MATE_IN_MAX_PLY (= MATE_SCORE-128 = 28872) and INSIDE the TB band (> TB_WIN = 28800). Such a score is not recognized by is_mate_score (no mate display, excluded from the aspiration mate skip), is not clamped by the NMP mate clamp (`null_score.abs() > MATE_IN_MAX_PLY`, line 3702), and masquerades as a definite TB win/loss to any TB-range reasoning. The score_to_tt ply adjustment still applies (threshold TB_WIN-200 = 28600), so TT round-trip is unbroken — the corruption is band misclassification only.
finding.evidence: Line 5169: `return -MATE_SCORE + ply;` inside the QS evasion path, with ply unbounded by MAX_PLY (only `qs_safe_ply = (ply as usize).min(MAX_PLY - 1)` clamps the stack INDEX at 5092, not the score). tt.rs:592: `pub const MATE_IN_MAX_PLY: i32 = MATE_SCORE - crate::search::MAX_PLY as i32;` = 28872; tt.rs:578 `TB_WIN = 28800`. QS entry from negamax possible at any ply <= 127 (dispatch at 3348), plus up to 32 qs_depth levels (4954, 5150, 5360 pass ply+1).
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness, near-zero frequency (requires a mate discovered beyond seldepth 128 inside a QS chain); fix is trivial and removes a latent band-corruption source.
finding.suggested_change: Clamp the ply used for mate construction in qsearch (`-MATE_SCORE + ply.min(MAX_PLY as i32)`), or add a `ply >= MAX_PLY → return eval` guard at qsearch entry mirroring negamax's 2985.

finding.title: ZW TT window narrowing not gated on halfmove_ok: at halfmove >= 89 the node continues with an inverted window (alpha > beta) and TT-stores the incoherent result at full depth
finding.claim: At zero-window nodes the TT 'window narrowing' ALWAYS collapses the window: for TT_FLAG_LOWER, `tt_score > alpha` with beta = alpha_orig+1 implies tt_score >= beta, so `alpha = tt_score` makes alpha >= beta; symmetrically for UPPER. The only consumer, the collapse-return at 3270, is gated on `halfmove_ok` (halfmove < 89), but the narrowing itself is NOT. So for every node with halfmove in [89, 99] holding a matching TT bound, the search proceeds through the whole node with alpha >= beta (possibly alpha >> beta, e.g. alpha=500 vs beta=11). Children are then searched with inverted windows (-beta, -alpha) where their alpha > beta: razoring fires against the inflated alpha (3562), futility prunes almost every quiet against it (4204), and child RFP fires against a hugely deflated beta returning eval-margin values far from truth. The resulting best_score is classified against the pre-narrowing alpha_orig at 4839 and stored in the TT at full depth (4851) — the P2 gate was added precisely because near-50mr scores are unsafe, but this path manufactures fresh incoherent scores and stores them anyway. Trace: ZW node (alpha=10, beta=11), halfmove=92, TT LOWER tt_score=500 with sufficient depth → first cutoff branch skipped (halfmove_ok false, 3196-3198) → 3258 sets alpha=500 → 3270 `alpha >= beta && halfmove_ok` false → move loop runs with (500, 11) window → children searched at (-11, -500) → TT store at depth d.
finding.evidence: Lines 3256-3268: `TT_FLAG_LOWER => { if beta - alpha_orig == 1 && tt_score > alpha { alpha = tt_score; } } TT_FLAG_UPPER => { if beta - alpha_orig == 1 && tt_score < beta { beta = tt_score; } }` — no halfmove gate. Line 3270: `if alpha >= beta && halfmove_ok {` — return gated. Line 3176: `let halfmove_ok = (board.halfmove as i32) < tp(&TT_CUTOFF_HALFMOVE_MAX);` (default 89, search.rs:508). Store: lines 4838-4851 `let flag = if best_score <= alpha_orig { TT_FLAG_UPPER } ... info.tt.store(board.hash, depth, store_score, flag, best_move, raw_eval, tt_pv);` — not gated on window sanity.
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness; plausibly small LTC Elo in shuffle/conversion endgames (halfmove 89-99 is exactly the regime of the documented won-position-draw conversion failures). Fix is one condition.
finding.suggested_change: Gate the narrowing on halfmove_ok as well (`if beta - alpha_orig == 1 && halfmove_ok && ...`), or equivalently skip the whole narrowing block when !halfmove_ok — at ZW the narrowing is purely a collapse-then-return mechanism, so there is nothing to salvage from it near the 50-move cliff.

verdict.reasoning: Verified line-by-line in src/search.rs. The ZW TT window narrowing (3256-3268) is gated only on `beta - alpha_orig == 1`, and at ZW it can never merely 'bias': LOWER with tt_score > alpha forces alpha = tt_score >= beta; UPPER symmetrically forces beta <= alpha. The in-code rationale ('Window-narrowing is still applied — it only biases the search', lines 3173-3175) is mathematically wrong for the only window shape the narrowing applies to. The collapse-return at 3270 and the direct cutoff at 3196 are both gated on halfmove_ok (hm < 89, tunable at line 508), so for hm in [89,99] with a matching sufficient-depth TT bound the node proceeds with alpha >= beta. Downstream confirmed: razoring (3562) and futility (4204) fire against the inflated alpha; first move is searched at the literally inverted window (-beta,-alpha) at line 4595; PVS re-search conditions (4578/4587) are unsatisfiable with alpha >= beta so scout results at the untrusted bound are accepted directly; the TT store (4843-4856) has no window-sanity gate and in the UPPER case classifies LOWER against the mutated (deflated) beta at 4846. alpha_orig is captured post-MDP at 3146, so the reviewer's precondition (alpha == alpha_orig at the narrowing) holds. One detail corrected: only the FIRST move gets an inverted child window; non-first moves get coherent (-alpha-1,-alpha) null windows centered on the untrusted TT bound — the node is still incoherent either way, since P2's whole point was that this bound is unreliable near the 50-move cliff, and the node never searches the true (alpha_orig, alpha_orig+1) window. Reachable in practice: shuffle/conversion endgames routinely revisit positions at hm 89-99 with deep TT entries — the exact regime of docs/conversion_failure_study_2026-06-29.md. Suggested fix (gate narrowing on halfmove_ok) is correct: at ZW the narrowing exists solely to feed the collapse-return, so when the return is gated off there is nothing to salvage. Caveats: expected Elo is small and LTC is the diagnostic frame (cf. #2418 mate-score fix: STC inert/H0, LTC H1 +0.7; and #2416 fired ~1600x/game yet measured neutral — a firing mechanism does not guarantee Elo). Bench will change (tree shape). No other-engine citations in the finding to spot-check.
