finding.title: Non-PV first-move child searched with cut_node=false instead of !cut_node
finding.claim: The 'first move: always full window' branch hardcodes the child's cut_node to false. At a non-PV ALL node (cut_node=false), the first child is an expected CUT node and every reference engine passes !cutNode there; Coda passes false, mislabeling the entire leftmost spine of every all-node subtree. This directly disables three cut_node-gated features on that spine: NMP (search.rs:3656 `&& cut_node` — the Reckless gate, meaning NMP can never fire at these mislabeled expected-cut nodes), IIR (search.rs:3750 `(is_pv || cut_node)`), and the TT-cutoff node-type guard (search.rs:3196 `cut_node == score_above_beta && bound_matches` — legitimate lower-bound TT cutoffs are rejected because the node claims to be an all-node), plus the SE negative-extension cut-node branch (search.rs:4143) degrades to the weaker branch. The code contradicts Coda's own convention comment at search.rs:2949: 'cut_node: bool, // true at expected cut nodes (child of all-node, non-first child of PV)'. The line dates unchanged to the original GoChess translation (commit 2ff2b77); the 2026-06-23 LMR audit verified re-search polarity ('cut_node propagation in re-searches (!cut_node): correct') but never checked this first-move branch, and no experiment in experiments.md has ever touched it. Verified against current main: the branch reads `score = -negamax(board, info, -beta, -alpha, new_depth, ply + 1, false);` while the PVS zero-window path at 4589 correctly passes `!cut_node`.

All 6 references route non-PV first moves through a zero-window branch with !cutNode: Stockfish search.cpp:1283-1292 `else if (!PvNode || moveCount > 1) ... value = -search<NonPV>(pos, ss+1, -(alpha+1), -alpha, newDepth - ..., !cutNode);`; Obsidian search.cpp:1108-1109 `else if (!IsPV || seenMoves > 1) score = -negamax<false>(newPos, -alpha-1, -alpha, newDepth, !cutNode, ss+1);`; Reckless search.rs:852-894 `else if !NODE::PV || move_count > 1 { ... -search::<NonPV>(td, -alpha-1, -alpha, reduced_depth, !cut_node, ply+1) }`; Berserk search.c:750-751 `else if (!isPV || playedMoves > 1) score = -Negamax(-alpha-1, -alpha, newDepth-1, !cutnode, ...);`; PlentyChess search.cpp:859-861 and Alexandria search.cpp:859-861 `else if (!pvNode || totalMoves > 1) { score = -Negamax<false>(-alpha-1, -alpha, newDepth, !cutNode, td, ss+1); }`. 6/6 agree against Coda. (Note: passing false IS correct for the PV full-window calls, and coincidentally correct when the parent is a cut node; the divergence is exactly at all-node parents.)

finding.title: No persistent root-move list: partial-iteration root results are always discarded on stop — including a proven aspiration fail-high move; all 6 reference engines keep a sorted RootMoves array whose partial-iteration scores remain usable
finding.claim: Coda treats the root as an ordinary negamax node: best_move is taken from pv_table[0][0] only after a COMPLETED iteration, and on any mid-iteration stop the stable_pv snapshot from the previous iteration is restored and everything the partial iteration learned is thrown away. Concrete traced case: when a root aspiration search completes with `result >= beta` (fail-high), pv_table[0][0] holds the proven-better move (set at 4622 on the root beta cutoff), but the loop widens beta and re-searches (2373-2379); negamax resets pv_len[0]=0 at entry (2960), so if should_stop fires during the widened re-search, the break at 2389-2397 restores stable_pv from the LAST COMPLETED ITERATION — discarding a move the just-completed fail-high search proved scores >= beta at the current depth. This costs exactly at time pressure, where the newly discovered move is most often a tactical save. More broadly, all six reference engines maintain a persistent RootMoves vector with per-move scores, stable-sorted after every root search call, so (a) a best move proven in a partial iteration is used ('The score of any root move is updated only if search wasn't yet stopped... usable at any time' — Obsidian), and (b) root moves 2..N are ordered by previous-iteration score rather than generic history. Since a timed search is almost always stopped mid-iteration, the deepest (partial) iteration is the most expensive one and Coda systematically discards its root-level conclusions. Coda's conservative restore was motivated by a real PV/ponder consistency bug (comment at 2255-2261), but the consensus fix is a root-move structure, not wholesale discard.
finding.evidence: Coda: fail-high path 2373-2379 does not touch best_move; on stop `if info.should_stop() { if stable_pv_len > 0 { info.pv_len[0] = stable_pv_len; ... } break; }` (2389-2397); best_move extraction at 2411 `if info.pv_len[0] > 0 { let pv_move = info.pv_table[0][0]; ... best_move = m; }` only reached when the iteration completed; root ordering is fallback + TT-move only (2266-2282); root cutoff sets pv at 4621-4628. Stockfish search.cpp:376-382: `std::stable_sort(rootMoves.begin() + pvIdx, ...)` after every aspiration call, with the comment that sorting keeps partial results valid on stop; bestmove comes from rootMoves[0]. Obsidian search.cpp:1395-1397: root-move scores 'usable at any time' + sortRootMoves(pvIdx). Reckless search.rs:136-141: `td.root_moves[...].sort_by_key(...)` after each root search, before the stopped check. Berserk search.c:279 `SortRootMoves(thread, thread->multiPV);` inside the aspiration loop. PlentyChess search.cpp:1462 `sortRootMoves();` inside the loop. Alexandria keeps pvTable/rootmove score updated per completed root move. 6/6 on the other side.
finding.expected_impact: +1-3 Elo guess (partial-iteration best-move usability + score-ordered root moves), concentrated at LTC/time-pressure; the fail-high-only fix alone is ~+0.5-1.5 and cheap; full RootMoves is a larger implementation but enables MultiPV
finding.suggested_change: Cheap incremental fix: inside the aspiration loop, after a COMPLETED (not stopped) search with result >= beta, capture pv_table[0][0], validate it against root_legal (same matching as 2417-2424), and update best_move immediately; keep the stable_pv restore for the PV tail (ponder consistency unaffected since best_move and pv_table[0][0] then agree). Full consensus fix: add a RootMoves array (move, score, prev_score, pv) updated at ply==0 whenever a root move completes its full-window re-search; stable-sort per aspiration call; take bestmove/ponder from rootMoves[0] with its PV snapshotted at proof time (preserving the ponder-consistency fix). Enables MultiPV as a side effect.

Adjacent only: "fix-root-history" (root-only history table) H0'd 3x — #124 (-0.8, 5320g), #142 retry (-7.9, 1800g, "DROP permanently"), Day-6 lesson "root ordering already good" — which weakens the score-ordered-root-moves-2..N half of the expected impact but not the primary fail-high/partial-iteration mechanism. The stable_pv restore itself is a deliberate ponder-consistency fix (lichess oeZ7KRUt forfeit, 2026-04-26), acknowledged by the reviewer.
verdict.reasoning: Every code claim traced accurately. best_move only updates after a completed iteration (search.rs:2411-2443); the aspiration fail-high branch (2373-2379) never captures pv_table[0][0], which at that point provably holds the fail-high move (root PV set on score>alpha before the beta-cutoff return, ~4616-4631); negamax wipes pv_len[0] at entry (~2953); a stop during the widened re-search hits the break at 2389-2396, restores stable_pv from the LAST COMPLETED iteration, and returns the old best_move (2937). Hunted for neutralizers and found none: the TT fallback (2426-2443) is unreachable on the stop path, there is no post-loop TT rescue, and SMP vote aggregation cannot help (helpers share the discard structure; OB is Threads=1). The broader claim also holds: a trustworthy mid-iteration alpha-raise at root (completed subtree before stop fired in a later sibling) is discarded by the same restore. Spot-checked 3 of 6 engine citations, all accurate: Stockfish search.cpp:382 stable_sorts rootMoves BEFORE the stop-break with the exact quoted comment; Reckless search.rs:136 sorts root_moves before "if td.stopped { break; }"; Obsidian search.cpp:1396-1397 has the "usable at any time" comment. Genuine 6/6-consensus structural gap. Caveats on magnitude: the fail-high-then-stop window is narrow (root fail-highs are infrequent and the TT-ordered re-search usually re-proves quickly), and the root-history prior ("root ordering already good", H0 x3) suggests the ordering half of the win is small — so expect the low end of +1-3, concentrated at LTC/time-pressure, which is exactly Coda's diagnosed weak regime (gap is TM + LTC-scaling). The cheap incremental fix (capture proven fail-high move into best_move after a COMPLETED search, keep stable-PV tail restore so best_move and pv_table[0][0] agree — ponder consistency preserved) is low-risk; suggest SPRT at [0,3], ideally with LTC given the mechanism. The full RootMoves rewrite is justified mainly if MultiPV is wanted; its incremental Elo over the cheap fix is more speculative.

finding.title: Correction history trains on the PRE-correction eval error; 5/6 reference engines train on the residual error AFTER correction (negative feedback)
finding.claim: Coda updates all five corrhist tables with err = best_score - scaled_eval, where scaled_eval is the halfmove-scaled but UNCORRECTED eval (and the direction-consistency gates at 4875-4878 also compare against scaled_eval). SF, Reckless, Obsidian, PlentyChess and Alexandria all train on bestScore/bestValue minus the CORRECTED static eval (ss->staticEval after correction was applied), i.e. each table learns only the error the current blend failed to explain. That residual form is a negative-feedback loop that self-normalizes across correlated sources; Coda's open-loop form drives every table independently toward the full error, so positions where several sources are simultaneously 'hot' (e.g. pawn-corr and both np-corr on the same structure) get double-counted, and calibration rests entirely on the SPSA weights /CORR_HIST_DIV being right on average. Berserk is the one reference engine on Coda's side (trains on rawEval), so this is 5-vs-1 consensus, not unanimous. Coda's comment at 4888-4893 justifies the halfmove-scaling choice but never addresses the pre-vs-post-correction choice.
finding.evidence: Coda: `update_correction_history(info, board, best_score, scaled_eval, depth);` (search.rs:4893) with `let err = search_score - raw_eval;` (1473, where the arg is scaled_eval = pre-correction); gates `best_score < scaled_eval` etc. (4875-4878). Stockfish search.cpp:1495-1499: `bonus = std::clamp(int(bestValue - ss->staticEval) * depth * ...` where ss->staticEval = to_corrected_static_eval (747). Reckless search.rs:1085-1089: `update_correction_histories(td, depth, best_score - eval, ply);` where eval = correct_eval (414). Obsidian search.cpp:1229-1230 (adjustEval, 824); PlentyChess search.cpp:1268-1270 (correctStaticEval, 757); Alexandria search.cpp:930-934 (adjustEval, 515). Counterexample: Berserk search.c:819-820 `UpdatePawnCorrection(rawEval, bestScore, ...)` uses raw.
finding.expected_impact: quality / possible small Elo; direction uncertain (Berserk counterexample; SPSA weights partly absorb the miscalibration)
finding.suggested_change: Pass static_eval (corrected) instead of scaled_eval to update_correction_history and to the direction-consistency gates, matching the 5-engine residual form. Likely wants a corrhist-weight cluster retune-on-branch afterwards; SPRT [0,3].

Coda: search.rs:3414-3416 shows scaled_eval is halfmove-scaled PRE-correction and static_eval = corrected_eval(scaled_eval); line 4893 passes scaled_eval to update_correction_history, whose err = search_score - raw_eval (1473) is therefore best_score minus the uncorrected eval; the direction gates at 4875-4878 also use scaled_eval. No neutralizing guard anywhere (QS only reads corrhist, never updates; TT stores raw_eval so no interaction). The comment block covers only halfmove-scaling, not the correction choice — this is not a documented deliberate choice. All six engine citations spot-checked and accurate: SF (search.cpp:1496-1501, ss->staticEval = to_corrected_static_eval at 747), Reckless (search.rs:1089, eval = correct_eval at 414/417; the one later eval=tt_score reassignment at 449 is in_check-only and excluded by the update gate), Obsidian (1229, adjustEval at 824), PlentyChess (1269, correctStaticEval at 750/757), Alexandria (934, adjustEval at 504/515) all train on the residual after correction; Berserk (search.c:819-820) genuinely uses rawEval — but Berserk-13 is a single-table pawn-corrhist, where the multi-table double-counting argument doesn't even apply, so the counterexample is weaker than 5-vs-1 suggests. finding.title: ProbCut child searches read and WRITE cont-hist under a stale ply slot (moved_piece_stack never set in the ProbCut loop)
finding.claim: Every other recursion site maintains the cont-hist context stack: the main move loop sets info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u]/moved_to_stack[ply_u] before make_move (4157-4160), both QS paths set it (5129-5135, 5339-5346), and NMP zeroes it before its null search (3628, 3687). The ProbCut loop makes a move and recurses into quiescence (3831) and negamax at pc_depth (3835) at ply+1 WITHOUT writing the stack. The child then reads moved_piece_stack[ply_u] as its 'parent move' — which still holds whatever move was last written into that slot by an unrelated sibling subtree at the same ply. Concrete path: at ply p, sibling node A searches Nf3 (slot p := knight/f3); search returns; later at the same ply p node B (different position) runs ProbCut, makes QxR, recurses to p+1; the child's negamax (3882-3888) builds prev_piece_for_cont = knight/f3, its MovePicker cont_hist_subs[0] points at cont_hist[N][f3], and on every beta cutoff in that subtree it WRITES bonuses/maluses into cont_hist[N][f3][...] cells (4680-4694) for a continuation that never happened — polluting the shared table, not just misreading it. Stockfish explicitly sets ss->continuationHistory in its ProbCut do_move.
finding.evidence: Coda ProbCut loop (search.rs:3820-3835): `if !board.make_move(mv) {...} ... let mut score = -quiescence(board, info, -probcut_beta, -probcut_beta + 1, ply + 1); if score >= probcut_beta && pc_depth > 0 { score = -negamax(..., pc_depth, ply + 1, !cut_node); }` — no moved_piece_stack/moved_to_stack write anywhere in the loop, unlike the main loop at 4157-4159: `info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u] = go_piece(moved_piece) as u8; info.moved_to_stack[ply_u] = to;`. Child read at 3882-3888: `let gp = info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u - 1] ...`. Stockfish search.cpp:979 `do_move(pos, move, st, ss)` -> search.cpp:576-583: `ss->currentMove = move; ss->continuationHistory = &continuationHistory[ss->inCheck][capture][dirtyPiece.pc][move.to_sq()];` inside the ProbCut loop; do_null_move likewise resets to the sentinel.
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness; +Elo guess 0-2 (cont-hist pollution scales with ProbCut volume at LTC depths)
finding.suggested_change: After make_move succeeds in the ProbCut loop, mirror the main loop: `if ply_u <= MAX_PLY { info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u] = go_piece(pc_moved_piece) as u8; info.moved_to_stack[ply_u] = move_to(mv); }` (capture the mover with board.piece_at(from) before make_move). SPRT [-2,1] or bundle with another small fix.

verdict.reasoning:
The claim survives every attack; all cited details check out.

CODE (src/search.rs): The ProbCut loop (3805-3867) calls `board.make_move(mv)` at 3820 and recurses into `quiescence(..., ply + 1)` at 3831 and `negamax(..., pc_depth, ply + 1, ...)` at 3835 with NO write to `info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u]` / `moved_to_stack[ply_u]` anywhere in the loop. A full grep of all stack writes confirms the only writers are: RFP-audit null (3628-3629), NMP null sentinel (3687-3688), main move loop (4157-4159), QS evasion path (5132-5133), QS capture path (5343-5344). The arrays are reset only at search start (1998, 2137), not per node, so at a ProbCut node the slot almost always holds the (piece,to) of whatever unrelated sibling subtree last searched a move at the same ply. The `gp != 0` guard at 3885 does not neutralize it — stale values are nonzero real pieces. Consequences confirmed: (a) child negamax reads slot ply_u as its parent move (3883-3884) and passes the stacks to MovePicker (3912-3914), so cont-hist move ordering and the LMR history adjustment in the entire ProbCut verification subtree use a fabricated continuation key; (b) on beta cutoffs the child WRITES bonuses into cont_hist[stale_piece][stale_to][...] at 4680-4694 (also 4555, 4726 — offsets 1/2/4/6, so descendants at ply+2/+4/+6 also hit the stale slot), polluting the shared table; (c) the ProbCut qsearch child also reads the stale stack via MovePicker::new_evasion (5087-5096). Path is trivially reachable — ProbCut fires at every eligible non-PV depth>=~5 node.

REFERENCE ENGINES (both spot-checked, both accurate): Stockfish search.cpp:979 uses `do_move(pos, move, st, ss)` in the ProbCut loop, and do_move (563-584) sets `ss->currentMove` and `ss->continuationHistory` exactly as the finding quotes; do_null_move sets the sentinel. Reckless search.rs:603 uses its shared `make_move(td, ply, mv)` in the ProbCut loop, and make_move (1351-1365) sets `td.stack[ply].mv/.piece/.conthist`. Coda's ProbCut is the ONLY recursion site in the codebase that bypasses stack maintenance.

PRIOR ART (experiments.md): No prior test of this exact ProbCut site — grep for probcut × stack/sentinel/cont-hist finds nothing. But the identical bug CLASS has been found and fixed twice before, which strongly corroborates the mechanism: (1) C3 audit 2026-04-22, #640/#668 "NMP was leaving moved_piece_stack[ply_u] stale; children read polluted cont-hist keys" — merged as confident-correctness at −1.6 Elo H0 @ 19874g, explicitly noted as "load-bearing for downstream cont-hist-sensitive experiments"; (2) the QS evasion-chain stale-stack fix (comment at 5127-5131). The NMP code's own comment (3681-3685) describes this exact failure mode. Precedent also warns on Elo expectations: the NMP sentinel fix H0'd mildly and the companion stale-reductions fix (#646 −5.1 H0) only turned positive (+2.8 H1, #670) after retune — so expect near-neutral raw Elo, possibly needing retune-on-branch.

CORRECTED DETAIL (minor): unlike the NMP fix (zero sentinel), the right fix here is to write the actual ProbCut move — `info.moved_piece_stack[ply_u] = go_piece(pc_moved_piece)` (captured via board.piece_at(from) BEFORE make_move) and `moved_to_stack[ply_u] = move_to(mv)` — matching the main loop at 4157-4159 and SF/Reckless semantics. Bench will change (tree shape), so per the bug-fix bounds precedent submit at [-2,1] and treat as a retune candidate if it H0s near the boundary, per the #668/#670 pattern.

finding.title: Helper threads are never seeded with trans_corr (the one corrhist table missing from the copy list)
finding.claim: The helper-spawn seeding copies pawn_corr, np_corr and cont_corr from the main thread with an explicit comment 'seed helpers from main's accumulated corrections', but trans_corr — added later (CORR_W_TRANS, Cinder idea, weight 74 of the ~628 total corrhist weight) — was never added to the list. Helpers are respawned per `go`, so every search each helper runs with the transition-correction component zeroed while main runs with its warm, persistent (never cleared per-go) table. The threads therefore compute systematically different corrected static evals for identical positions, and store them into the shared TT — exactly the divergence class the codebase elsewhere works to avoid (cf. the threat_stack mirroring comment at 1647-1649: 'helpers must evaluate consistently with main, otherwise shared-TT entries disagree'). trans_corr is 2*16384*4B = 128KB — the '~260 KB total — cheap' comment shows cost was not the reason for omission.
finding.evidence: search.rs:1673-1678: `// T2.1/T2.4: ... seed helpers from main's accumulated corrections (~260 KB total — cheap, unlike the ~13 MB pawn_hist which stays unseeded). helper.pawn_corr.copy_from_slice(&main.pawn_corr[..]); helper.np_corr.copy_from_slice(&main.np_corr[..]); helper.cont_corr.copy_from_slice(&main.cont_corr[..]);` — no trans_corr line. Field exists at 903-904: `/// Transition correction history: [stm][(hash(ply-1) ^ hash(ply)) % size] trans_corr: Box<[[i32; CORR_HIST_SIZE]; 2]>` and is read in corrected_eval at 1436-1442 with weight tp(&CORR_W_TRANS) (default 74, tunables line 259). clear_correction_history (1162) does clear it, confirming it is considered part of the corrhist set everywhere except the seeding site.
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness (SMP-only, small: helpers relearn trans_corr per go); ship-if-not-regression class
finding.suggested_change: Add `helper.trans_corr.copy_from_slice(&main.trans_corr[..]);` at search.rs:1678. Bench-identical at Threads=1; verify with a T>1 non-regression SPRT [-2,1] or bundle with another SMP-touching change.

finding.title: TT-cutoff cont-hist malus fires unconditionally — SF/Obsidian/Alexandria all gate it on the previous node's moveCount < 4
finding.claim: Coda's TT-cutoff malus (penalize the opponent's last quiet move when a TT hit proves the resulting position fails high) applies on EVERY qualifying TT cutoff. All three reference engines that have this exact feature — including Alexandria, the explicitly cited source of Coda's port — additionally require that the opponent's move was among the first few tried at its parent (moveCount < 4 / seenMoves <= 3). The gate's semantics: only demote a HIGHLY-RANKED move that walked into a known-lost position; when a late, already-low-ranked move did so, the malus is noise (the position was likely already lost and the ordering info content is nil). TT cutoffs are the most frequent cutoff class, so the ungated version writes maluses at very high volume into cont-hist. Coda cannot currently express the gate — there is no per-ply move-count stack (only the local `move_count`). IMPORTANT prior-art caveat: this site has 4 H0s (#2490, #169, #672, #2316) covering existence, indexing, bonus/malus symmetry, and magnitude rescale — experiments.md declares 'TT-cutoff cont-hist malus audit closed'. The moveCount-gate axis is the one axis those tests did NOT touch, and it is the axis where all three feature-havers agree; but the H0 history means expected magnitude is small and a regression would confirm the closed verdict.
finding.evidence: Coda search.rs:3229-3234: `if score_above_beta && stack_len >= 2 && ply_u >= 2 { ... if opp_undo.mv != NO_MOVE && opp_undo.captured == NO_PIECE_TYPE && our_undo.mv != NO_MOVE { ... malus ... } }` — no condition on how early the opponent's move was at its node. Stockfish search.cpp:794-795 (TT cutoff block): `if (prevSq != SQ_NONE && (ss - 1)->moveCount < 4 && !priorCapture) update_continuation_histories(ss - 1, pos.piece_on(prevSq), prevSq, -2014);`. Obsidian search.cpp:751-757: `if (ttScore >= beta && prevSq != SQ_NONE && !(ss-1)->playedCap && (ss-1)->seenMoves <= 3) { addToContHistory(chIndex, -statMalus(depth), ss-1); }`. Alexandria search.cpp:477 (Coda's cited source): `if (ttMove && ttScore >= beta && (ss-1)->moveCount < 4 && isQuiet((ss-1)->move))`. Corroboration: Reckless's analogous prior-refutation malus at beta cutoff, search.rs:1024-1027, gates on `td.stack[ply - 1].move_count < 2`. Coda sides with zero of the four.
finding.expected_impact: elo-opportunity, 0 to +1.5 Elo class; also unlocks a per-ply move_count stack that Reckless-style prior-move features need
finding.suggested_change: Add a small `move_count_stack: [u16; MAX_PLY+1]` written where moved_piece_stack is written (search.rs:4157-4160, plus the null-move sentinel at 3687), and gate the malus at search.rs:3232 with `info.move_count_stack[ply_u - 1] < 4`. finding.title: QS depth-cap (qs_depth >= 32) returns static eval even when in check; all 6 references return draw/0 in check at the ply cap

When the capped node is in check, this returns an NNUE eval of an in-check position — a state the net is never trained on (training filters keep quiet positions) and which every reference engine refuses to evaluate at its ply cap, returning draw/0 instead (the side may in fact be getting mated). finding.title: halfmove >= 100 returns draw before checkmate detection — mate delivered on the 100th halfmove scored as 0
finding.claim: Both QS and negamax return draw_score for halfmove >= 100 unconditionally, before check/evasion/checkmate detection. FIDE rules (and cutechess/OB adjudication) score a checkmate delivered by the move that completes the 50-move period as a WIN — the mate takes precedence over the draw (explicit in the Art. 9.6 automatic-rules wording; SF implements `rule50_count() > 99 && (!checkers() || MoveList<LEGAL>(pos).size())`). Concrete path: parent node at halfmove=99 plays a quiet checkmating move; child enters quiescence (or negamax) with halfmove=100, side to move in checkmate; line 4970 `if board.halfmove >= 100 { return draw_score; }` fires before the in-check evasion loop's `if move_count == 0 { return -MATE_SCORE + ply; }` (5168-5170) can run, so the parent scores its mate-in-1 as 0. Symmetrically, Coda may rely on the 50-move rule to 'escape' a mate that actually ends the game.

finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness; ~0 Elo (requires a quiet mating move landing exactly on halfmove 100), but changes game results vs adjudicators in that case. Fix is a cheap gate: only return the rule-50 draw if not (in check with no legal moves); bounds [-2,1]
finding.suggested_change: At both sites: `if board.halfmove >= 100 && !(board.checkers() != 0 && no_legal_moves) { return 0; }` — cheapest form: when halfmove>=100 AND in check, fall through to the evasion loop/movegen (which returns mate on move_count==0) and re-check the draw after at least one legal move is found.

finding.title: LMR reduction floored at 0 — negative adjustment sums can never extend, unlike 5/6 references
finding.claim: Coda clamps `reduction` to [0, new_depth-1], so its many reduce-less signals (gives-check -1, tt_pv -1, escape -1, improving -1, history/LMR_HIST_DIV, complexity/LMR_COMPLEXITY_DIV, threat-density, king-pressure, root-depth relaxation) saturate at zero: a move that is simultaneously checking, previously-PV, well-historied, and in a complex position gets exactly the same depth as a merely-average early move. 5 of 6 references clamp the reduced depth to newDepth+1 or newDepth+2 (or an explicit lmr-extension), letting a strongly negative adjustment sum grant the move a 1-2 ply search EXTENSION beyond the first-move depth; only Berserk sides with Coda (it floors R at 1 and caps at newDepth). Compounding this, Coda only enters the adjustment block at all when the base table value is > 0 (`if reduction > 0`), so at base 0 the signals are never even summed — the extension headroom is structurally unreachable. Neither the LMR audit (its clamp note only covers the new_depth-1 floor re-clamp) nor experiments.md contains a test of allowing reduced_depth > new_depth.

References: Stockfish search.cpp:1258 `Depth d = std::max(1, std::min(newDepth - r / 1024, newDepth + 2)) + PvNode;` (up to +2, +1 more at PV); Obsidian search.cpp:1090-1091 `// Clamp to avoid a qsearch or an extension in the child search` — `int reducedDepth = std::clamp(newDepth - R, 1, newDepth + 1);` (+1); Reckless search.rs:829-832 `let lmr_extension = reduction < -3072 && move_count <= 3; (new_depth - reduction / 1024).clamp(1, new_depth + 1 + lmr_extension as i32) + 2 * NODE::PV;`; PlentyChess search.cpp:1125 `std::clamp(newDepth - reduction, 100, newDepth + lmrPotentialExtension) + lmrPvNodeExtension * pvNode` (lmrPotentialExtension=105 ≈ +1 ply); Alexandria search.cpp:835-836 `int reducedDepth = std::max(1, std::min(newDepth - depthReduction, newDepth)) + pvNode;` (+1 at PV only). Berserk search.c:732-733 `R = Min(newDepth, Max(R, 1));` sides with Coda. 5/6 allow >= +1 extension headroom.

finding.title: Evasion ordering: captures only softly separated from quiets (10000 offset) — SF/Berserk/Obsidian enforce strict captures-first in check
finding.claim: In evasion scoring, captures get `10000 + mvv_lva + capt_hist` while quiet evasions get the full quiet-history sum (main ±16384, plus cont-hist at plies 1/2 weighted by CONT_HIST_MULT≈3 over i16 entries clamped ±32000, plus pawn-hist × PAWN_HIST_MULT). Two inversions follow that no reference engine with dedicated evasion ordering allows: (a) a capture with strongly negative capt-hist (down to −16384) scores ~−4800 and sorts BELOW ordinary quiets; (b) a hot quiet (main ~12k + weighted cont-hist) exceeds 10000+mvv+0 and sorts ABOVE a fresh capture of the checker. The three reference engines that special-case evasion ordering all make the capture/quiet separation unconditional — the capture band cannot be crossed by any history value. Reckless (no evasion special-case) still stages SEE-good noisy strictly before all quiets. In-check nodes are common (every check in the tree), and capturing/blocking the checker is the dominant refutation, so soft separation adds first-move-cut noise exactly where the move set is small and the best move is usually tactical. I found no experiments.md entry probing this offset (only the QS evasion quiet-ordering bug fix, line 918).

Berserk movepick.c:81-82: `else if (type == ST_EVASION_CAP) current->score = 1e7 + SEE_VALUE[captured];` — same unconditional band. Coda is the only implementation where history can reorder across the capture/quiet boundary while in check.

finding.title: QS pays SEE twice per capture: picker good/bad partition + loop-level QS_SEE_THRESHOLD gate
finding.claim: Non-check quiescence uses MovePicker::new_quiescence, whose generate_and_score_captures runs `see_ge(board, m, -capt_hist/18)` on EVERY generated capture to partition good/bad (movepicker.rs:533-534). The QS loop then runs a second, independent `see_ge(board, mv, tp(&QS_SEE_THRESHOLD))` (default -26) on every picked move (search.rs:5327) before searching it. So each capture that gets picked costs two full SEE walks, and the partition verdict is discarded. Worse, the delta-prune (5311-5321) and the move-count budget (5303) run AFTER picking, so captures that were going to be delta-pruned anyway still paid the partition SEE at generation time. QS is the majority of nodes, and SEE is one of the more expensive per-move primitives. References run one SEE gate in QS: SF prunes with a single !pos.see_ge(move) in qsearch and its QS movepicker does not SEE-partition; Coda's own main-search picker partition at least feeds ordering (bad captures last), but in QS the loop's threshold re-check makes the partition's pruning content redundant — its only surviving value is the good-before-bad ordering, which a score offset could preserve without the second SEE.

finding.title: QS lacks the consensus 'eval+margin <= alpha => prune non-material-winning captures' futility clause
finding.claim: Coda's only QS futility form is the victim-value delta prune: `stand_pat + see_value(cap_pt)*SEE_MATERIAL_SCALE/100 + QS_DELTA_MARGIN <= alpha` (search.rs:5318-5319), plus a static SEE gate `see_ge(mv, QS_SEE_THRESHOLD=-26)` (5327). It has NO clause that prunes captures which merely don't WIN material when the stand-pat is hopelessly below alpha. Consequence: in desperate positions (eval far below alpha) Coda still searches every SEE-clean capture, including equal trades (QxQ has SEE~0, and its delta value stand_pat+1200*2.15+368 almost always clears alpha), even though an equal trade cannot raise eval back above alpha. 5 of 6 reference engines have exactly this clause as their (or one of their) QS futility prunes, and Reckless achieves the same effect by scaling its SEE threshold with the alpha-eval gap. This is a structural missing prune, not a constant delta; it was NOT covered by the 2026-06-24/25 QS audit (which ruled out only a QS_SEE_THRESHOLD constant change, quiet-checks, max-captures, and TT-move ordering).

References: Stockfish search.cpp:1674-1678 `if (!pos.see_ge(move, alpha - futilityBase)) { bestValue = std::max(bestValue, std::min(alpha, futilityBase)); continue; }` (futilityBase = staticEval+328, line 1625); Obsidian search.cpp:585-588 `if (!isQuiet && !pos.checkers && futility <= alpha && !pos.seeGe(move, 1)) { bestScore = std::max(bestScore, futility); continue; }` (futility = bestScore + QsFpMargin, line 545); Berserk search.c:922-925 `if (!inCheck && mp.phase != QS_PLAY_QUIET_CHECKS && futility <= alpha && !SEE(board, move, 1)) { bestScore = Max(bestScore, futility); continue; }` (futility = bestScore + 63, line 901); PlentyChess search.cpp:532-535 `if (futilityValue <= alpha && !SEE(board, move, 1)) { bestValue = std::max(bestValue, futilityValue); continue; }` (futilityValue = staticEval + qsFutilityOffset, line 501); Alexandria search.cpp:1049-1053 `const int futilityBase = ss->staticEval + qsBaseFutility(); if (futilityBase <= alpha && !SEE(pos, move, 1)) { bestScore = std::max(futilityBase, bestScore); continue; }`. Corroboration Reckless search.rs:1225 `if !td.board.see(mv, (alpha - eval) / 8 - 100)` — the SEE bar rises as eval falls below alpha, same mechanism folded into one test. All 6 on the 'gap-aware prune' side; Coda alone has only a static SEE bar.

finding.title: In-check QS searches every capture evasion with zero SEE/bad-capture pruning

finding.title: QS delta prune is not fail-soft: pruned-move value never raised into best_score, so stored UPPER bounds are incorrectly tight
finding.claim: When Coda delta-prunes a capture it just `continue`s; best_score stays at stand_pat. The pruned move's true value can be up to stand_pat+victim+margin (that is the prune's own upper estimate), i.e. strictly above best_score. The node then stores TT_FLAG_UPPER with score best_score (5379-5389) — an upper bound claim that the pruned move can violate. Later probes at a different alpha can take an UPPER cutoff (5051-5052) on this too-tight bound. Every reference engine that has a value-based QS futility prune raises bestValue to the futility value when pruning (fail-soft max), exactly to keep the returned/stored upper bound sound; SF does it in the clause that is the exact analog of Coda's victim-value delta prune. Coda is the sole engine with a value-based QS prune and no max-update. (Coda's QS_MAX_CAPTURES budget skip also doesn't update, but neither do the peers' moveCount prunes — only the value-based prune is the divergence.)
finding.evidence: Coda (search.rs:5318-5321): `stand_pat + see_value(cap_pt) * tp(&SEE_MATERIAL_SCALE) / 100 + tp(&QS_DELTA_MARGIN) <= alpha { continue; }` — no best_score update; store at 5389 `info.tt.store(board.hash, -1, store_score, flag, best_move, raw_stand_pat, false)` with `flag = ... else TT_FLAG_UPPER`. References: Stockfish search.cpp:1662-1670 `futilityValue = futilityBase + PieceValue[pos.piece_on(move.to_sq())]; if (futilityValue <= alpha) { bestValue = std::max(bestValue, futilityValue); continue; }` — same victim-value shape, WITH the max; Obsidian search.cpp:586 `bestScore = std::max(bestScore, futility);`; Berserk search.c:923 `bestScore = Max(bestScore, futility);`; PlentyChess search.cpp:533 `bestValue = std::max(bestValue, futilityValue);`; Alexandria search.cpp:1051 `bestScore = std::max(futilityBase, bestScore);`. Reckless has no value-based clause (SEE-only) so is neutral. 5-of-5 engines with the clause sit on the max-update side.
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness (sounder QS UPPER bounds in TT) plus small Elo; cheap to bundle with the missing QS futility clause
finding.suggested_change: In the delta prune: compute `let fut = stand_pat + see_value(cap_pt) * tp(&SEE_MATERIAL_SCALE) / 100 + tp(&QS_DELTA_MARGIN); if cap_ok && fut <= alpha { best_score = best_score.max(fut); continue; }` (bench changes only via TT contents; SPRT [0,3] or bundle with the new futility clause).

verdict.reasoning: Code verified line-by-line: the QS delta prune (search.rs:5311-5322) bare-continues without raising best_score, and the node stores TT_FLAG_UPPER with best_score at 5379-5389; the UPPER consumer paths (QS TT cutoff at 5051-5052 requiring tt_score <= alpha, and stand-pat UPPER refinement at 5232-5237) make the too-tight bound consequential. Reachability confirmed: with SEE_MATERIAL_SCALE=215 and QS_DELTA_MARGIN=368 the prune fires only when alpha - stand_pat >= ~583cp (fail-low nodes, exactly where UPPER stores happen); alpha is raised to best_score at 5266-5268 so the max-update is only a no-op when alpha_orig <= stand_pat — the fail-low case where it matters is common. No neutralizing guard found. Reference citations spot-checked and accurate for 3 of 5: Stockfish search.cpp:1662-1670 (exact victim-value analog WITH bestValue = max(bestValue, futilityValue)), Obsidian search.cpp:584-588, Berserk search.c:921-925 — all max-update on their value-based QS prune; the reviewer's parenthetical that peers' moveCount/SEE prunes also skip without updating is also accurate, so the claimed divergence is precisely scoped. One correction: the "incorrectly tight bounds / correctness bug" framing is overstated — fail-soft bounds under heuristic pruning are never sound (Coda's SEE prune at 5327 also skips without max-update, matching peers), and Coda's fut is a deliberately inflated threshold (2.15x victim + 368), so this is a multi-engine consensus structural gap with plausible small Elo via TT UPPER-bound quality, not a hard bug. Implementation note: max-updating with the 215-scaled fut pushes stored UPPER bounds nearly to alpha (much looser than SF's 1x-victim analog); consider also testing the max with 100-scale victim value. Priority medium rather than high: it is a verified consensus gap, but the effect is TT-bound-quality only in already-failing-low QS nodes, and the recent QS audit banked the larger QS TT wins already; expect small Elo, cheap one-line SPRT at [0,3] (bench changes via TT contents).

finding.title: Non-capture promotion beta cutoff takes the QUIET history path: writes tables the picker never reads for promos, leaves the read caphist[*][*][0] bin permanently zero, and breaks the quiet-malus off-by-one exclusion
finding.claim: At both cutoff history-update sites, the quiet/noisy split is `if !is_cap` (capture/EP only, no promotion term), so a non-capture promotion that causes a beta cutoff is bonused as a QUIET: it writes main butterfly history, cont-hist and pawn-hist. But the movepicker classifies promotions as NOISY on the read side: they are generated exclusively in the captures stage (movegen.rs:138-143 'Non-capture promotions' inside generate_captures; generate_quiets is 'non-captures, non-promotions') and scored by `mvv_lva() + capt_hist_score_static()`, where capt_hist_score_static reads `history.capture[piece][to][0]` (empty-victim bin) for non-capture promos. That bin is NEVER written anywhere — the capture-bonus branch requires `captured_pt != NO_PIECE_TYPE` (4768), captures_tried requires the same (4284-4285), and the TT-cutoff caphist site's ct=0 arm (3305) is unreachable because tt_is_cap requires a victim. Three consequences: (a) zero learned ordering signal for non-capture promos; (b) main[from][to] is piece-agnostic, so a b7b8=Q cutoff inflates the ordering/futility-hist_adj score of any quiet Rb7-b8/Kb7-b8 later (cross-piece pollution); (c) the malus loop `for i in 0..quiets_count.saturating_sub(1)` (4707) assumes the cutoff move is the last quiets_tried entry, but promotions are never pushed (4277 gates on `!is_cap && !is_promo`), so on a promo cutoff the last genuinely-FAILED quiet is silently spared its malus. The internal inconsistency — tracking excludes promos while the update classifier is `!is_cap` alone — shows this is accidental, not carved. Coda's own #1670 (fix/tt-move-classifiers-promo, H1 +2.5) already established that 'promotions consistently noisy' pays at other classifier sites; this is the same fix class applied to the history-update sites, which #1670 did not touch (verified in its diff, commit b5bc93a).

Picker read side movepicker.rs:906-924 `capt_hist_score_static` returns `history.capture[go_piece(piece)][to][0]` when victim is NO_PIECE_TYPE and not EP (exactly non-capture promos); movepicker.rs:939-958 scores promos in the capture scorer. Reference engines all route promotions through the NOISY update path so read and write bins coincide: Stockfish search.cpp:1857 `if (!pos.capture_stage(bestMove))` — capture_stage includes queen promotions, so a promo cutoff updates `captureHistory[movedPiece][to][capturedPiece=NO_PIECE]`, the same bin its movepicker reads; Reckless search.rs:1001 `if best_move.is_noisy()` (is_noisy includes promotions) → noisy_history with captured=None bin, same bin scored in movepick; Obsidian position.h:154 isQuiet excludes promotions, search.cpp:1185 `if (pos.isQuiet(bestMove))` else captureHistory; Alexandria splits via isQuiet/isTactical (search.cpp:913-916, isTactical at 931) with promos in noisyMoves. Route noisy cutoffs through the capture-history bonus with ct = captured_type(victim) or 0 for non-capture promos (drop the `captured_pt != NO_PIECE_TYPE` guard, keep piece/to indexing with the pre-move pawn as SF/Reckless do), add non-capture promos to the noisy-tried malus list, and make the quiet-malus exclusion conditional on the cutoff move actually being the last pushed quiet. verdict.reasoning: Every load-bearing claim verified in the code. (1) search.rs:3971 is_cap = victim||EP with no promo term; the cutoff split at 4638 `if !is_cap` sends a non-capture promotion down the QUIET bonus path (main hist 4666, cont-hist 4687, pawn-hist 4700). finding.title: Correction history trains on PRE-correction error (open-loop integrator; consensus trains on residual)
finding.claim: Coda updates all five corrhist tables with err = best_score - scaled_eval, where scaled_eval is the PRE-correction static eval (halfmove-scaled NNUE only, per the three-variable doc at search.rs:3359-3364). The direction gates (4875-4878) also compare against scaled_eval. All three strongest references train on the POST-correction residual (bestValue - correctedStaticEval), which is what makes corrhist a negative-feedback loop: as the table learns, the residual shrinks and updates stop. Training on the pre-correction error is open-loop: for any position class with a persistent same-sign eval bias, the update bonus never shrinks no matter how well the table already corrects, so the gravity equilibrium of update_corr_entry (*entry += bonus - *entry*|bonus|/1024) is entry -> +/-CORR_HIST_LIMIT (1024) for ANY constant-sign bias, however small — solving bonus = entry*|bonus|/1024 gives entry* = +/-1024 independent of bias magnitude. Correction magnitude is therefore governed by the cap/weights (up to ~50cp at saturation with current weights) rather than tracking the actual bias: small biases get slowly wound up toward maximum correction (overshoot), and the applied correction feeds RFP/futility/LMR-complexity/SE-margin everywhere. The nearby comment only justifies scaled-vs-raw (halfmove decay), not pre-vs-post correction — the divergence looks unexamined rather than deliberate.

Reckless search.rs:414+1089: `eval = correct_eval(td, raw_eval, correction_value); ... update_correction_histories(td, depth, best_score - eval, ply);` (gates also use corrected `eval`). Obsidian search.cpp:824+1229: `eval = ss->staticEval = adjustEval(pos, rawStaticEval, ss); ... bonus = clamp((bestScore - ss->staticEval) * depth / 8, ...)`.

finding.title: Aspiration window centered on last iteration score instead of a running average
finding.claim: Coda centers the aspiration window on the raw previous-iteration score (`prev_score`). 4 of 6 references (Stockfish, Reckless, Berserk, Alexandria — including both #1 and #2) center the window on a RUNNING AVERAGE of iteration scores, updated as avg = (avg + value)/2 after each in-window resolve; the remaining two (Obsidian, PlentyChess) still size the window width from a mean/meanSquared score even though they center on the last value. Mechanism: iteration scores oscillate (odd/even depth parity, tactical flips); centering on the last value chases the oscillation and triggers more fail-high/fail-low re-search cycles, while the average damps it. Coda has neither an average-centered window nor an average-sized delta (delta uses prev_score² too).
finding.evidence: Coda search.rs:2352-2355: `let avg = prev_score; let mut delta = tp(&ASP_DELTA) + (avg*avg / tp(&ASP_SCORE_DIV));  let mut alpha = (prev_score - delta)...` — 'avg' is just the last score. Stockfish search.cpp:354-357: `delta = 5 + threadIdx % 8 + std::abs(rootMoves[pvIdx].meanSquaredScore) / 10208; Value avg = rootMoves[pvIdx].averageScore; alpha = std::max(avg - delta, ...)` with averageScore updated at :1330-1331 `(value + rm.averageScore) / 2`. Reckless search.rs:118-121 centers on `average[td.pv_index]`, updated at :156-160 `(average + score) / 2`. Berserk search.c:257-265: `int score = thread->rootMoves[thread->multiPV].avgScore; alpha = Max(score - delta, ...)`. Alexandria search.cpp:272-273: `score = AspirationWindowSearch(averageScore, ...); averageScore = averageScore == SCORE_NONE ? score : (averageScore + score) / 2;` and :353 `alpha = std::max(-MAXSCORE, prev_eval - delta)` where prev_eval = averageScore. Obsidian search.cpp:1378-1386 and PlentyChess search.cpp:1449-1453 center on last score but size the window from avgScore²/meanScore².
finding.expected_impact: +1-3 Elo (fewer aspiration re-searches on oscillating evals); one local variable, easily SPRT-able
finding.suggested_change: Keep a per-search running average: `avg = if first { score } else { (avg + score) / 2 }` updated on each in-window resolve; center alpha/beta (and the delta² term) on avg instead of prev_score, in both search() and search_helper().

finding.title: 50-move-rule draw return lacks the checkmate exception: a mate delivered on the 100th halfmove is scored as 0 — all 6 reference engines verify not-mated before returning the rule-50 draw
finding.claim: Both negamax and qsearch return draw_score=0 unconditionally when `board.halfmove >= 100`. Under FIDE rules (and every adjudicator, including cutechess/lichess), checkmate takes precedence: if the move that produced the 100th halfmove delivers mate, the game is a win, not a draw. Trace: opponent plays a quiet checkmating move that is the 100th halfmove → Coda's child node enters negamax with halfmove==100, in check, zero legal moves → returns 0 at line 2972-2974 instead of `-MATE_SCORE + ply` (the checkmate detection at 4816-4819 is unreachable because the draw return fires first; checkers are only computed later at 3354) → the parent scores the mating line as a draw. Dangerous both ways: when losing near the 50-move boundary Coda can 'escape' into a line it scores 0 that the arbiter scores as Coda being checkmated; when winning it avoids a mate landing exactly at halfmove 100 because it reads as a draw. All six reference engines gate the rule-50 draw on 'not in check, or at least one legal move exists'; the check is free in practice because it only runs when halfmove>=100.
finding.evidence: Coda negamax: `if board.halfmove >= 100 { return draw_score; }` (search.rs:2972-2974), same in quiescence (4970-4972) — no checkers/legal-move test. Stockfish position.cpp:1523: `if (st->rule50 > 99 && (!checkers() || MoveList<LEGAL>(*this).size())) return true;`. Reckless board.rs:283-285: `self.halfmove_clock() >= 100 && (!self.in_check() || self.has_legal_moves())`. Obsidian position.cpp:112-118: `if (halfMoveClock < 100) return false; if (!checkers) return true;` then generates evasions. Berserk board.c:555-562: `if (board->fmr > 99) { if (board->checkers) { RootMoves(moves, board); return moves->count > 0; } ...}`. PlentyChess search.cpp:408-414 and Alexandria search.cpp:46-56: same not-checkmate gate with comments. 6/6 on the other side.
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness; rare edge case (~0-0.5 Elo, requires mate exactly at the halfmove-100 boundary) but the failure mode is a full point, and the fix is cheap and consensus-backed.
finding.suggested_change: Gate the halfmove>=100 draw return on `checkers == 0 || at least one legal move exists` in both negamax and quiescence (compute checkers lazily, only when halfmove>=100): `if board.halfmove >= 100 && (board.checkers() == 0 || has_legal_move(board)) { return 0; }`. SPRT [-2,1] as a correctness fix.

Believability probe: instrumented fall-through + niced depth-12 self-play (120 games) → fired ~1,600×/game in pawnless mating endgames — so the mechanism is very live, but the search already found those mates via other lines, so correcting the classification changed almost no games' results. Merge only if rule-correctness is valued for its own sake; there is no strength argument and a hair of measured downside at the tightest CI in the wave." finding.title: Every QS capture pays SEE twice: picker good/bad partition + the QS SEE gate
finding.claim: In the non-check QS loop, MovePicker::generate_and_score_captures already ran `see_ge(board, m, -capt_hist/18)` on every generated capture to partition good/bad (used only for ORDER in QS — both stages are iterated), and then the QS loop re-runs `see_ge(board, mv, QS_SEE_THRESHOLD=-26)` on every non-pruned move. Since see_ge is monotone in threshold, the second call is provably redundant whenever the picker threshold was >= -26 (i.e. capt_hist <= 468: pass at t>=-26 implies pass at -26; classified bad at t>=-26 implies fail at... the bad-stage still needs the gate only when capt_hist>468). QS nodes are 25% of the tree and this is their hot loop. Separately, `board.is_legal(mv, ...)` at 5292 runs BEFORE the move-count budget (5303), delta pruning (5311) and the SEE gate (5327), so every pruned capture also pays a legality check it never needed (legality is only required before make_move; SF checks legal() last).
finding.evidence: movepicker.rs:531-534: `let capt_hist = capt_hist_score_static(...); ... let see_threshold = -capt_hist / 18; if !see_ge(board, m, see_threshold) { // Bad capture`. search.rs:5327: `if !see_ge(board, mv, tp(&QS_SEE_THRESHOLD)) { continue; }` (QS_SEE_THRESHOLD default -26, search.rs:505). Loop order search.rs:5292 `if !board.is_legal(mv, qs_pinned, qs_checkers) { continue; }` precedes 5303 budget, 5311 delta prune, 5327 SEE gate.
finding.expected_impact: +Elo guess: ~0.5-1% NPS in QS-heavy positions; NPS-only class, SPRT [-2,1]
finding.suggested_change: Have the QS-mode picker cache a per-move 'passes QS threshold' verdict (compute see_ge once against min(see_threshold, QS_SEE_THRESHOLD) plus a bit for the gap band), or simply partition with QS_SEE_THRESHOLD in new_quiescence mode so good-stage moves skip the gate entirely (TT move still gated). Also reorder the loop to budget -> delta -> SEE -> is_legal.

NPS optimization. Result: -2 Elo (49.7%, 376-385-605, 1366 games). Killed — flat zero. Notes: Theory was sound (avoid double SEE for good captures, skip bad captures entirely). But the NPS gain from one fewer SEE call per QS capture is negligible.' Also relevant caution: #1947/checking-sqs lesson (~15450) that bench-identical recompute-elimination perf items repeatedly measure flat-to-negative; QS audit 2026-06-24/25 (~16328) ruled out 'QS SEE-threshold change (no signal)' without SPRT.
verdict.reasoning: Mechanism CONFIRMED in code: MovePicker::new_quiescence (movepicker.rs:306-341) sets skip_quiet=true, so the stage machine (451-484) iterates GoodCaptures then BadCaptures — both stages reach the QS loop, so the picker's see_ge(m, -capt_hist/18) at movepicker.rs:533-534 is ordering-only in QS. The QS loop then re-runs see_ge(mv, QS_SEE_THRESHOLD=-26) at search.rs:5327 on every move surviving legality/budget/delta. Monotonicity math checks out (see_ge is a threshold test; pass at t implies pass at any t' <= t): the second call is provably redundant for good captures with capt_hist <= 468 and for bad captures with capt_hist >= 468. Reference check: Stockfish's QS picker (movepick.cpp QCAPTURE_INIT/QCAPTURE stages) runs NO SEE at all — the single see_ge(move, -73) in qsearch is its only SEE — so single-SEE-per-QS-capture is genuinely what the #1 engine does. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) The is_legal-ordering sub-claim's SF citation is WRONG — current SF qsearch checks pos.legal(move) FIRST, immediately after next_move() and before all pruning (search.cpp:1644), exactly Coda's order (search.rs:5292 before budget 5303/delta 5311/SEE 5327). The reorder is behavior-neutral and might save a little, but has no consensus backing; Coda matches SF. Note Coda's QS is_legal was itself a deliberate 2026-06 audit correctness addition (comment at 5286-5291). (2) Magnitude is likely below the reviewer's 0.5-1% guess: see.rs:41-53 shows see_ge early-exits on the balance fast paths for most clear-good captures, so the redundant call is usually a few subtractions, not an iterative exchange. WHY ONLY LOW/RETEST: the direct prior (2026-03-12) tested removing the redundant loop SEE and measured flat, though it (a) bundled a tree-shape change (skipping bad captures entirely, which the finding's cache-verdict variant avoids), (b) predates the current ~+300 Elo stronger engine, and (c) was only 1366 games. The dedup-with-cached-verdict variant preserving exact ordering and node counts is untested and cheap, but the project's repeated experience is that bench-identical recompute-elimination in this engine measures flat-to-negative.

finding.title: QS generates all four push-underpromotions, which are structurally exempt from every QS prune (budget + delta); top references generate queen-only pushes in noisy movegen
finding.claim: Coda's generate_captures emits all four promotion pieces (Q,R,B,N) for non-capture pushes to the 8th rank (add_promotions at movegen.rs:138-143 white, 187-192 black), and the QS capture loop exempts every promotion from BOTH the QS_MAX_CAPTURES budget (`&& !is_promotion(mv)` at search.rs:5305) AND delta pruning (`if !is_promotion(mv)` at 5311). The only remaining filter is the SEE gate at -26, which an undefended promotion square passes for all four pieces (quiet promo SEE balance = see_value(promo) - see_value(PAWN), e.g. +320 for a knight). So a QS node with an unopposed 7th-rank pawn spawns four unprunable promotion subtrees, three of which (R/B/N) are dominated by the queen promotion in a captures-only search — underpromotion only ever matters to avoid stalemate or deliver a knight check, and neither is representable in Coda's QS (no stalemate detection, no gives-check logic). This multiplies QS tree width by up to 4x exactly in the pawn-race endgames where QS chains are longest. Cross-engine: SF, Reckless and PlentyChess generate ONLY the queen promotion for pushes in their noisy/captures generator (underpromotion pushes are classified quiet and never reach QS when not in check); Obsidian sides with Coda (all 4). Capture-promotions with all 4 pieces ARE consensus — the divergence is specifically non-capture underpromotion pushes.
finding.evidence: Coda (movegen.rs:139-144): `let mut push_promo = ((pawns << 8) & empty) & promo_rank; while push_promo != 0 { ... add_promotions(&mut list, to - 8, to); }` where add_promotions pushes Q,R,B,N (movegen.rs:83-87). search.rs:5303-5308: `if qs_move_count >= qs_max_caps && best_score > -(MATE_IN_MAX_PLY) && !is_promotion(mv) { continue; }`; 5311: `if !is_promotion(mv) { ... delta prune ... }`. see.rs:36-38: `if is_promo { balance += see_value(promo_pt) - see_value(PAWN); }` — knight promo on an unattacked square yields SEE=+320 >= -26, so the gate at search.rs:5327 passes all four. References: Stockfish movegen.cpp:93-105 `if constexpr (Type == CAPTURES || all) *moveList++ = ...QUEEN; if constexpr ((Type == CAPTURES && Enemy) || (Type == QUIETS && !Enemy) || all) { ROOK/BISHOP/KNIGHT }` — push promos (Enemy=false) in CAPTURES get queen only; Reckless board/movegen.rs:147-155 `if T::KIND == Kind::Noisy { list.push_pawns_setwise(up, promotions, MoveKind::PromotionQ); } if T::KIND == Kind::Quiet { PromotionR/B/N }`; PlentyChess move.cpp:73-83 '// Queen promotions (without capture)' adds QUEEN only to the noisy list, underpromotions at move.cpp:47-49 are in quiet gen. Obsidian movegen.cpp:76-96 uses addPromotionTypes (all 4) for pushes — sides with Coda. Berserk not verified. 3 vs 2 among verified engines, with the top-2 (SF, Reckless) both queen-only.
finding.expected_impact: +Elo guess: small (0-2), concentrated in pawn-race endgames / long QS chains where QS depth matters most; cheap principled restriction
finding.suggested_change: Either generate queen-only push promotions in generate_captures (moving R/B/N pushes to generate_quiets so main search still sees them — verify perft after the movegen split), or the least-invasive form: skip non-queen promotions in the QS loop (`if is_promotion(mv) && move_flags(mv) != FLAG_PROMOTE_Q { continue; }`), keeping evasion mode untouched, where underpromotions can be the only legal evasion. At minimum stop exempting non-queen promotions from the QS budget/delta prune. SPRT [0,3].

In the QS loop, promotions are exempt from BOTH the move-count budget (search.rs:5303-5305 '&& !is_promotion(mv)') and delta pruning (5311 'if !is_promotion(mv)'), leaving only the SEE gate at -26 (5327). see.rs:36-38 gives a quiet promo balance of see_value(promo)-see_value(PAWN), so a knight push-promo to an UNDEFENDED square is +320 (N=420, P=100 per eval::see_value) and passes; on a defended square balance-risk goes negative and the iterative SEE typically fails it, so the 4x-subtree blowup is confined to undefended promo squares — consistent with the finding's own framing. Cross-engine citations SPOT-CHECKED AND ALL CORRECT: Stockfish movegen.cpp make_promotions — CAPTURES gets QUEEN unconditionally, R/B/N only 'if (Type == CAPTURES && Enemy)' i.e. capture-promos only; Reckless board/movegen.rs:147-154 — Noisy pushes PromotionQ only, R/B/N are Kind::Quiet; PlentyChess move.cpp generatePawn_capture — '// Queen promotions (without capture)' adds QUEEN only, R/B/N push-promos live in the quiet generator; Obsidian movegen.cpp:93 uses addPromotionTypes (all 4, lines 9-15) for pushes — sides with Coda as stated. The movegen-split alternative needs perft re-verification and main-search movepicker awareness (R/B/N pushes must move to generate_quiets). Expected magnitude is small and concentrated in pawn-race endgames, but it is a cheap, genuinely untested consensus alignment with the top engines: SPRT [0,3] as proposed.

finding.title: max_nodes limit never sets the stop flag — partial 0-scores are stored to TT/history on node-limited searches
finding.claim: should_stop()'s node-limit branch returns true WITHOUT storing the shared stop flag, unlike both time branches (lines 1127, 1151 do self.stop.store(true)). Every downstream guard that suppresses partial results keys off the stop FLAG, not off should_stop(): the TT store at 4838 (`!info.stop.load()`), the corrhist update at ~4886, and the per-move `if info.stop.load() { return 0 }` unwind. Consequence on `go nodes N`: once global_nodes >= N, negamax entries return 0 (score corruption) but stop stays false, so every ancestor on the unwind completes its move-loop epilogue treating those 0s as real child scores and STORES the polluted best_score/best_move into the TT at full claimed depth (and can fire fake beta-cutoff history bonuses when beta <= 0). These poisoned entries persist for the rest of the game (TT is shared across `go`). Concrete trace: `go nodes 100000` → uci.rs:1208 sets limits.nodes → search.rs:2247 max_nodes → at a node where `info.nodes & 1023 == 0`, should_stop() hits line 1116, returns true → negamax line 3057 `return 0` (before `info.nodes += 1`, so the counter freezes on the boundary and all sibling negamax entries also return 0) → parent at line 4612 treats 0 as the child score → line 4838 guard passes because stop was never stored → `info.tt.store(...)` writes the corrupted entry. Additionally the comment at 1113-1114 ('all threads stop together') is wrong today: helpers have max_nodes==0 so their gate never fires, and with stop never stored they only halt when search_smp:1937 finally sets it.
finding.evidence: search.rs:1116-1118: `if self.max_nodes > 0 && self.global_nodes.load(Ordering::Relaxed) >= self.max_nodes { return true; }` — no `self.stop.store`. Contrast the time paths, 1126-1128: `if self.abs_deadline > 0 && elapsed >= self.abs_deadline { self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed); return true; }` and 1150-1152 identically. TT store guard, 4838: `if info.excluded_move[ply_u] == NO_MOVE && !info.stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {` — explicitly documented as 'skip if search was stopped — partial results corrupt the TT', but the node-limit path never trips it. Negamax abort site 3055-3057: `if info.nodes & 1023 == 0 && info.should_stop() { return 0; }` with `info.nodes += 1` only afterwards (3064).
finding.expected_impact: bugfix-correctness — affects any node-limited search (`go nodes`, fixed-node testing, node-odds); TT poisoning carries into subsequent moves of the same game. No effect on time-based SPRT/bench.
finding.suggested_change: In the max_nodes branch of should_stop(), mirror the time branches: `self.stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed); return true;`. This also makes helpers actually stop at the node limit (shared flag) and re-arms the existing partial-result guards (TT store, corrhist, stable-PV restore) for node-limited searches. Trivial [-2,1] non-regression SPRT candidate (behavior-neutral for time-based play).

finding.title: SMP result selection picks a move, not a thread: vote override silently drops the ponder move, desyncs info/bestmove, and lacks proven-win/loss protection
finding.claim: Coda's Lazy-SMP result selection is a pure max-vote over summed (move -> depth*(score-min+14)) weights returning a bare MOVE; helpers return only `(nodes, mv, score, depth)` from join (line 1927), never their PV, and nothing updates info.pv_table[0]/last_score/completed_depth to match the winner. Two consequence classes. (1) Ponder/PV desync: when the vote picks a helper's move (exactly the case where voting adds value), uci.rs's belt-and-braces check `pv_consistent = ponder_legal && move_from(si.pv_table[0][0]) == move_from(best_move) ...` (uci.rs:704-706) fails BY CONSTRUCTION, so the engine emits `bestmove X` with NO ponder (uci.rs:720) — the lichess deployment (Threads>1 WITH ponder) forfeits its entire ponder benefit on every vote-override move, and the last-printed `info ... pv` line names a different move than the bestmove (GUI/analysis desync). References re-print the chosen thread's PV (Obsidian search.cpp:1527-1529, Reckless uci.rs:234-236). (2) Missing decisive-score guards: all 5 reference engines that vote (SF, Reckless, Obsidian, Berserk, PlentyChess; Alexandria doesn't vote) select a THREAD and wrap the vote in protections — proven win only replaced by a higher win score (shortest mate/TB conversion), a proven-win thread taken regardless of votes, never vote-switch to a proven-loss thread, and SF/Berserk refuse threads with truncated PVs (pv.size() <= 2). Coda's summed-vote can pick a longer mate when two helpers agree on mate-in-5 vs one thread's mate-in-3 (2*d*w5 > d*w3), and has no loss guard. Secondary edges: if main completed no iteration (main_depth==0, e.g. instant abs_deadline) but exactly one helper completed depth>=1, `thread_results.len() <= 1` (1959) returns main's movegen/TT fallback and discards the helper's searched result; and helper moves enter the vote raw while main's move is validated against the root legal list (2411-2425).
finding.evidence: Coda search.rs:1926-1927: helpers return `(helper.nodes, mv, helper.last_score, helper.completed_depth)` — no PV. search.rs:1962-1972: `let weight = *depth as i64 * (*score as i64 - min_score as i64 + 14); ... votes.iter().max_by_key(|(_, w)| *w).map(|(m, _)| *m).unwrap_or(main_move)` — returns a move only, no decisive-score cases, nothing updates si.pv_table/last_score to match. uci.rs:704-706: `let pv_consistent = ponder_legal && move_from(si.pv_table[0][0]) == move_from(best_move) && move_to(si.pv_table[0][0]) == move_to(best_move);` then uci.rs:717-721: `if pv_consistent { println!("bestmove {} ponder {}", ...) } else { println!("bestmove {}", ...) }`. References: Stockfish thread.cpp:383-406: `bestThreadInProvenWin ... if (newThreadInProvenWin && newThreadScore > bestThreadScore) bestThread = th;` / proven-loss branch / `betterVotingValue = thread_voting_value(th) * int(newThreadPV.size() > 2) > ...`. PlentyChess search.cpp:1591-1604: `// In case of checkmate, take the shorter mate ... // We have found a mate, take it without voting`. Obsidian search.cpp:1517-1523: `if (abs(bestScore) >= SCORE_TB_WIN_IN_MAX_PLY) { if (currScore > bestScore) bestThread = st; } else if (currScore >= SCORE_TB_WIN_IN_MAX_PLY) bestThread = st; else if (currScore > SCORE_TB_LOSS_IN_MAX_PLY && currVote > bestVote)`. Berserk search.c:147-170 (same shape incl. `pv.count > 2` guard). Reckless uci.rs:199-231: `if is_win(best...) return current > best; ... !is_loss(current...) && (current_vote > best_vote || ...)`.
finding.expected_impact: +Elo at Threads>1 with ponder (lichess deployment regime — OB can't measure it): recovers the forfeited ponder on every vote-override move, fixes GUI info/bestmove mismatch, and adds the consensus mate/loss guards. +0-2 Elo class plus ponder-hit recovery.
finding.suggested_change: Return (move, score, depth, pv[0..2]) per thread and select a best THREAD: proven-win → highest score wins outright; never vote-switch to proven-loss or pv_len<2 threads; otherwise max votes. Adopt the selected thread's 2-move PV + score into info (optionally re-emit one final `info` line) so uci.rs's ponder emit stays armed; cheap alternative for the ponder alone: probe the shared TT after the winning move. While there, validate helper moves against the root legal list and prefer a depth>0 helper result over main's depth-0 fallback in the `len() <= 1` early-out.

verdict.prior_experiments: none found (grep 'vote', 'voting', 'thread select' in experiments.md — no SMP-selection experiment)
verdict.reasoning: All sub-claims verified. search_smp (search.rs:1867-1973): helpers return only (nodes, mv, last_score, completed_depth) at 1925-1927 (search_helper's mv = raw info.pv_table[0][0] at 2074-2076, NOT validated against root_legal, unlike main's 2411-2425 validation); vote at 1962-1972 is pure summed max returning a bare Move with no proven-win/loss cases and nothing updating si.pv_table[0]/last_score/completed_depth. uci.rs:673-706 verified: pv_consistent requires si.pv_table[0][0] from/to == best_move — fails by construction on any vote override → line 720 emits bestmove with NO ponder, and the last-printed info pv (from main) names a different move. finding.title: Aborted-iteration root results (including completed aspiration fail-highs) are discarded; all 6 references bank them
finding.claim: When should_stop fires mid-iteration, Coda restores the previous iteration's stable PV and keeps the previous iteration's best_move, discarding ALL results of the aborted iteration — including a NEW best root move that was already fully searched (root PV update at 4620-4628 happens atomically before the stop check, and negamax returns 0 on stop at 4608 before any further update, so pv_table[0] is internally consistent at abort). All 6 reference engines use the partial iteration's root results (with unproven-loss guards). Mechanism: the aborted iteration is the deepest and most expensive one; hard-stops correlate with fail-low/TM-extension positions where the deepest search just found a rescue move — Coda throws exactly that away and plays the known-worse previous move. A specific high-value sub-case: when an aspiration search COMPLETES with result >= beta (root fail-high — a move proven >= beta by a fully completed, non-stopped search), Coda records nothing (2373-2379 widens beta and re-searches without capturing pv_table[0][0]); if the hard limit fires during the re-search, the restore reverts to the previous iteration's move even though the fail-high move sits in pv_table[0][0] and is exactly the move most engines would play. This bites precisely on fail-high/fail-low turbulence — the searches that overrun the soft budget, i.e. the positions where the new information says the old best move is no longer best. The stable-PV mechanism (added for the lichess oeZ7KRUt ponder-consistency forfeit) only needs best_move and pv_table[0] to stay consistent — it does not require discarding completed results.
finding.evidence: Coda search.rs:2392-2396 on abort: `if stable_pv_len > 0 { info.pv_len[0] = stable_pv_len; for i in 0..stable_pv_len { info.pv_table[0][i] = stable_pv[i]; } } break;` and best_move is only updated after a completed iteration (2411: `if info.pv_len[0] > 0 { let pv_move = info.pv_table[0][0]; ... }` runs only when the loop was NOT broken). Fail-high branch 2373-2379 widens beta and loops without capturing pv_table[0][0]; root beta-cutoff PV write 4621-4628 `info.pv_table[ply_u][0] = mv; ... info.pv_len[ply_u] = 1 + child_len;` proves the fail-high move was available. References all use partial results: Stockfish search.cpp:382-388 sorts rootMoves then `// If search has been stopped, we break immediately. Sorting is safe because RootMoves is still valid, although it refers to the previous iteration` — bestmove comes from rootMoves[0] which includes completed root-move updates of the aborted iteration; Obsidian search.cpp:1395-1401 `// The score of any root move is updated only if search wasn't yet stopped... This means that the root moves' score is usable at any time` then `goto bestMoveDecided` using rootMoves[0]; Reckless search.rs:136-140 sorts root_moves BEFORE `if td.stopped { break; }`, and search.rs:204-211 adds the only guard (restore last_best_rootmove when aborted AND score is a loss); Alexandria search.cpp:219/313-316 takes GetBestMove() from the triangular pvTable at abort (no revert); Berserk search.c:315 `Move bestMove = thread->rootMoves[0].move` after longjmp abort. None of the 6 revert to the previous iteration wholesale.
finding.expected_impact: +2-5 Elo class at LTC (aborts land on the deepest iteration; fail-low rescue moves and proven fail-high moves currently discarded)
finding.suggested_change: Two complementary pieces. (1) On mid-iteration abort: if pv_len[0] > 0 (a root move completed and raised alpha this iteration), take best_move = pv_table[0][0] (validated against root_legal) and keep pv_table[0] as-is; only restore stable_pv when pv_len[0] == 0; add a Reckless-style guard (if the partial best's score is an unproven loss, keep the previous move). (2) Inside the aspiration loop, when a search returns result >= beta with stop NOT set, snapshot best_move + pv_table[0] into stable_pv (validated the same way) before re-searching, so the later restore resurrects the fail-high move. Existing uci.rs ponder-legality belt-and-braces (uci.rs:666-706) already protects the ponder emit. SPRT [0,3].

finding.title: No persistent root-move list: root ordering across iterations relies solely on TT move + history
finding.claim: Coda's root is an ordinary negamax node ordered by the staged movepicker (TT move first, then captures/history); there is no root-move array carrying per-move score/previousScore/avgScore/PV across iterations. 5 of 6 references (SF rootMoves, Reckless root_moves, Obsidian rootMoves, Berserk rootMoves, PlentyChess rootMoves; Alexandria is the one exception and instead keeps a dedicated rootHistory) maintain exactly this structure and re-sort it every iteration/aspiration attempt by (score, previousScore). Mechanism: (a) after a root fail-low, the replacement best is usually last iteration's #2-by-score, but Coda orders non-TT root moves by general history, so fail-low recovery searches root moves in a worse order at the highest-cost depth; (b) Berserk even primes the root 'hashMove' from the list (search.c:428 `hashMove = isRoot ? thread->rootMoves[thread->multiPV].move : hashMove`), immune to root TT-entry replacement, while Coda's root TT entry can be replaced/bound-polluted by helpers between iterations; (c) the structure is the natural enabler for the partial-abort banking, average-score windows, and thread-selection findings above (Coda already keeps root_move_nodes[4096] for TM — the list would subsume it).
finding.evidence: Coda has no root-specific ordering: negamax at ply==0 uses the same movepicker as interior nodes (root special-casing is limited to node accounting, search.rs:4485 `let nodes_before = if ply == 0 { info.nodes }` and 4603-4606 root_move_nodes update). References: Stockfish search.cpp:376-382 `std::stable_sort(rootMoves.begin() + pvIdx, ...)` per aspiration attempt (comment explains previousScore-preserving stable order); Reckless search.rs:97-99 `rm.previous_score = rm.score` each depth + :136/:171 sorts, and movepicker restricted to root_moves (search.rs:697); Obsidian search.cpp:1397/1427 sortRootMoves; Berserk search.c:249-250 previousScore carry + :279/:305 SortRootMoves + :428 root hashMove from list; PlentyChess search.cpp:1191 meanScore per root move. Alexandria: no root list (GetBestMove from pvTable, search.cpp:219) but adds rootHistory (search.cpp:268).
finding.expected_impact: +1-3 Elo direct (root ordering on fail-low recovery, immunity to root TT replacement); larger indirectly as the enabler for the abort-banking, average-window, and thread-selection findings
finding.suggested_change: Introduce a RootMove vec {mv, score, previous_score, avg_score, nodes, pv} built once per search; at ply==0 have the movepicker iterate this list in sorted order; stable-sort after each aspiration attempt; derive best_move/ponder/TM node-fraction/vote inputs from it.

finding.title: No root-score eval optimism (SF/Reckless/PlentyChess have it; Coda and 3 others don't)
finding.claim: The #1 (Stockfish), #2 (Reckless) and #5 (PlentyChess) engines derive a per-color 'optimism' term from the root move's average score at aspiration setup and blend it into static eval at every node (biasing eval toward the side the root says is winning, scaled by material/complexity). Obsidian, Berserk and Alexandria do not have it, and Coda has no trace of it (grep 'optimism' over src/ is empty). This is a 3-of-6 split rather than consensus, but the three holders include both engines above Coda's target cluster and the closest Rust structural reference, and Reckless adopted it from SF recently enough that it demonstrably pays below SF's level. Mechanism: contempt-like dynamic asymmetry that sharpens play when ahead and defends when behind, fed by the driver's root score.
finding.evidence: Stockfish search.cpp:359-361: `optimism[us] = 144 * avg / (std::abs(avg) + 91); optimism[~us] = -optimism[us];` (avg = rootMoves[pvIdx].averageScore). Reckless search.rs:123-127: `let best_avg = ((td.shared.best_stats[..].load(Ordering::Acquire) & 0xffff) as i32 - 32768 + average[td.pv_index]) / 2; td.optimism[td.board.side_to_move()] = 169 * best_avg / (best_avg.abs() + 187);` — note Reckless even SHARES the best root stats across SMP threads via an atomic for this. PlentyChess search.cpp:1438-1443: `int updatedOptimism = 150 * rootMoves[0].meanScore / (std::abs(rootMoves[0].meanScore) + 125);`. Absent in Obsidian/Berserk/Alexandria (grep 'optimism' over their src returns nothing) and in Coda (grep empty).
finding.expected_impact: +3-8 Elo potential per SF/Reckless adoption history, but requires eval-blend integration (nnue.rs) + likely retune-on-branch; medium risk. Note: distinct from the removed static contempt — this is score-adaptive, sign-symmetric, and eval-side

Prototype behind a tunable at 0 for a bench-neutral base.

finding.title: Helper threads respawned per `go` instead of a persistent thread pool
finding.claim: Coda spawns fresh helper threads (16MB stack, new SearchInfo, full history/corrhist copy from main, cold NNUE accumulator + Finny/refresh table, cold threat stack) on every `go`, and joins them at the end. All 6 references keep a persistent thread pool with an idle loop; each helper retains its OWN history, correction history, and accumulator refresh cache across moves. Consequences at Threads>1: (a) every helper's search-learned history/correction deltas from the previous move are discarded each move — all helpers restart from a clone of main's tables, reducing inter-thread diversity that Lazy SMP relies on (the same diversity rationale documented at search.rs:1975-1988 for helper aspiration); (b) per-move cold-start cost: N-1 thread spawns, ~260KB corrhist + history memcpy each, and a from-scratch Finny table rebuild per helper (the refresh-table cache is the expensive part at high Threads); (c) allocation churn per move. Single-threaded OB SPRTs never see any of this; the lichess multi-thread deployment pays it every move.
finding.evidence: Coda search.rs:1890-1928: `for thread_id in 1..threads { let mut helper = create_helper_info(info); ... std::thread::Builder::new().stack_size(16 * 1024 * 1024).spawn(...)}` and create_helper_info at 1628-1680 copies history (`helper.history.copy_from(&main.history)`) and corrhist per go. References: Obsidian threads.cpp:77 `searchThreads[index]->idleLoop();` with persistent `std::vector<std::thread*>` (:9); Berserk thread.c:100-151 ThreadInit allocates accumulators/refreshTable ONCE then `ThreadIdle(thread)` waits on a condvar; PlentyChess search.cpp:1539-1541 `void Thread::idleLoop()`; Stockfish thread.cpp ThreadPool with persistent Threads and per-thread state; Reckless threadpool.rs persistent ThreadPool with SharedContext; Alexandria keeps persistent ThreadData vector.
finding.expected_impact: +0-2 Elo at Threads>1 only (helper history persistence + warm Finny tables); zero effect on single-thread OB numbers, so validate via local multi-thread RR
finding.suggested_change: Keep N-1 helper SearchInfos alive across `go` commands (owned by the UCI thread alongside main's `si`), waking them per search; age their histories like main's instead of overwriting from main; only reset per-search scratch state as search_helper already does.

Zero effect on single-thread OB; validate via local multi-thread RR per the finding's own suggestion. Fair experiment, moderate implementation effort (ownership restructure of SearchInfo across go's).
